nodes.name: Untyped terms and substitutions with $\mathcal{W}$ (draft language)
nodes.statement: The sets of untyped terms and substitutions are defined inductively as follows: \begin{align*} M,N::&= x \mid MN \mid \lambda x. M \mid s\circ M \\ s,q::&= id \mid \mathcal{W} \mid \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x \rangle \mid s\circ q \end{align*} where the symbol $x$ denotes an arbitrary variable.
nodes.statement_short: Grammar of untyped terms (variables, application, abstraction, closure) and substitutions (id, W, cons, composition).

nodes.name: Typed terms and substitutions with $\mathcal{W}$ (draft language)
nodes.statement: The sets of typed terms and substitutions are defined inductively as follows: \begin{align*} M,N::&= x \mid MN \mid \lambda x^A. M \mid s\circ M \\ s,q::&= id \mid \mathcal{W} \mid \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x \rangle \mid s\circ q \end{align*} where $A$ is an arbitrary type.

nodes.name: Simultaneous substitution in the new notation
nodes.statement: A usual simultaneous substitution $$[x_1/N_1\,,\, x_2/N_2\,,\,\ldots\,,\, x_k/N_k]$$ in the new notation looks like $$\langle\ldots\langle\langle id\,,\, N_1\diagdown x_1\rangle\,,\, N_2\diagdown x_2\rangle\,,\,\ldots N_k\diagdown x_k\rangle$$ For brevity, we will write $$\langle id\,,\, N_1\diagdown x_1\,,\, N_2\diagdown x_2\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown x_k\rangle$$ But now any two (or more) of the variables $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ may coincide (as in contexts).
nodes.statement_short: The simultaneous substitution $[x_1/N_1,\ldots,x_k/N_k]$ is written $\langle id, N_1\diagdown x_1,\ldots,N_k\diagdown x_k\rangle$, with repeated variables allowed.

nodes.name: Judgement (typed)
nodes.statement: A \emph{judgement} is an expression of the form $\Gamma\vdash M:A$ or of the form $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$, where $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ are contexts, $A$ is a type, $M$ is a term, and $s$ is a substitution.

nodes.name: Typing rules
nodes.statement: (Typing rules).\\ $ \begin{array}{lll} (i)& \Gamma,x:A\vdash x:A &\\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{\Gamma\vdash x:A}{\Gamma,y:B\vdash x:A} & (x\not\equiv y) \\[15pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash M:A\rightarrow B}{\Gamma\vdash N:A}{\Gamma\vdash MN:B} &\\[15pt] (iv)& \ruleone{\Gamma,x:A\vdash M:B}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda x^A.M:A\rightarrow B} &\\[15pt] (v)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}{\Delta\vdash M:A}{\Gamma\vdash s\circ M:A} &\\[15pt] (vi)& \Gamma\vdash id\triangleright\Gamma &\\[5pt] (vii)& \Gamma,x:A\vdash\mathcal{W} \triangleright\Gamma &\\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}{\Gamma\vdash N:A}{\Gamma\vdash \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\triangleright\Delta\, ,x:A} &\\[15pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}{\Delta\vdash q\triangleright\Sigma}{\Gamma\vdash s\circ q\triangleright\Sigma} & \end{array} $\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Nine typing rules for terms and substitutions, with contexts allowing repeated variables and weakening only via rule (ii) and $\mathcal{W}$.
nodes.label: type

nodes.name: Example 1.2 (typing derivation)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruleone{x:A\,,\, x:B\vdash x:B}{x:A\,,\, x:B\,,\, y:C\vdash x:B} $$

nodes.name: Example 1.3 (typing derivation)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{x:A\,,\, x:B\vdash \mathcal{W}\triangleright x:A}{x:A\vdash x:A}{x:A\,,\, x:B\vdash \mathcal{W}\circ x:A} $$

nodes.name: Example 1.4 (typing derivation)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{x:A, x:B, y:C\vdash \mathcal{W}\triangleright x:A,x:B}{x:A, x:B\vdash \mathcal{W}\triangleright x:A}{x:A, x:B, y:C\vdash\mathcal{W}\circ\mathcal{W}\triangleright x:A}}{x:A\vdash x:A}{x:A, x:B, y:C\vdash (\mathcal{W}\circ\mathcal{W})\circ x:A} $$

nodes.name: Example 1.5 (typing derivation)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruleone{\ruleone{x:A\,,\, x:B\vdash x:B}{x:A\vdash\lambda x^B.x:B\rightarrow B}}{\vdash\lambda x^A.\lambda x^B.x:A\rightarrow(B\rightarrow B)} $$

nodes.name: Example 1.6 (typing derivation)
nodes.statement: $$\ruletwo{\Gamma,y:B\vdash\mathcal{W}\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{ \rule{5mm}{0mm} \Gamma\vdash M:A}}{\Gamma,y:B\vdash \mathcal{W}\circ M:A}$$

nodes.name: Explicit weakening reduces away when the variable is absent
nodes.statement: If the variable $y$ does not occur in the context $\Gamma$, then $\mathcal{W}\circ M$ reduces to $M$ in some sense (more precisely, $\mathcal{W}\circ M$ and $M$ have a common reduct).

nodes.name: Unique derivations for the typing rules
nodes.statement: The typing rules~\ref{type} have a pleasant property: every derivable judgement has a unique derivation.
conclusions: every derivable judgement has a unique derivation

nodes.name: Objects assigned to types
nodes.statement: Assume that some objects are assigned to types.

nodes.name: Object assigned to a context
nodes.statement: To each context of the form $$x_1:A_1 \,,\, x_2:A_2\,,\,\ldots\,,\, x_n:A_n$$ we assign the object $$(\ldots(\mathbf{1}\times A_1)\times A_2)\times\cdots)\times A_n)$$ where $\mathbf{1}$ is the (canonical) terminal object.
nodes.statement_short: A context $x_1:A_1,\ldots,x_n:A_n$ is interpreted as the left-nested product $(\ldots(\mathbf{1}\times A_1)\times\cdots)\times A_n$.

nodes.name: Diagrammatic composition notation
nodes.statement: Denote by $A\overset{f\,\circ\, g}{\rightarrow} C$ the composition of $A\overset{f}{\rightarrow}B$ and $B\overset{g}{\rightarrow}C$.

nodes.name: Arrow corresponding to a judgement (notation)
nodes.statement: $(\Gamma\vdash M:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\Gamma\overset{f}{\rightarrow} A$ is shorthand for ``the arrow $\Gamma\overset{f}{\rightarrow} A$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash M:A$."\\ $(\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\rightarrow} \Delta$ is shorthand for ``the arrow $\Gamma\overset{f}{\rightarrow} \Delta$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$."

B\overset{pr_1\,\circ\, f}{\rightarrow}A\using {\quad(x\not\equiv y)}}\\[20pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash M:A\rightarrow B)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\rightarrow}B^A}{(\Gamma\vdash N:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } \Gamma\overset{g}{\rightarrow}A}{(\Gamma\vdash MN:B)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{\langle f\,,\, g\rangle\,\circ\, Ev}{\longrightarrow}B}\\[20pt] (iv)& \ruleone{(\Gamma,x:A\vdash M:B)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } \Gamma\times A\overset{f}{\rightarrow}B}{(\Gamma\vdash\lambda x^A.M:A\rightarrow B)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{\Lambda (f)}{\rightarrow}B^A}\\[20pt] (v)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \triangleright\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\rightarrow}\Delta }{(\Delta\vdash M:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } \Delta\overset{g}{\rightarrow}A}{(\Gamma\vdash s \circ M:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } \Gamma\overset{f\,\circ\, g}{\rightarrow}A}\\[20pt] (vi)& (\Gamma\vdash id \triangleright\Gamma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{id}{\rightarrow}\Gamma \\[5pt] (vii)& (\Gamma,x:A\vdash\mathcal{W} \triangleright\Gamma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\times A\overset{pr_1}{\rightarrow}\Gamma \\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \triangleright\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\rightarrow}\Delta }{(\Gamma\vdash N:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{g}{\rightarrow}A}{(\Gamma\vdash \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle \triangleright\Delta\, ,x:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{\langle f\,,\, g\rangle }{\rightarrow}\Delta\times A}\\[20pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \triangleright\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\rightarrow}\Delta }{(\Delta\vdash q \triangleright\Sigma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Delta\overset{g}{\rightarrow}\Sigma }{(\Gamma \vdash s \circ q \triangleright\Sigma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f\,\circ\, g}{\rightarrow}\Sigma }\\ \end{array} $
nodes.statement_short: Categorical semantics: each derivable judgement is assigned an arrow of a cartesian closed category by induction on its unique derivation.
nodes.label: modeli

nodes.name: The calculus of equations
nodes.statement: (The calculus of equations).\\[5pt] $ \begin{array}{lll} (Beta) & (\lambda x.M)N= \langle id\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\circ M &\\ (Abs) & s\circ \lambda x.M=\lambda x.\langle \mathcal{W}\circ s\,,\, x\diagdown x\rangle\circ M &\\ (App) & s\circ (MN)=(s\circ M)(s\circ N) &\\ (ConsVar) & \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\circ x= N &\\ (New) & \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\circ y= s\circ y & (x\not\equiv y)\\ (IdVar) & id\circ x= x &\\ (Clos) & s\circ q\circ M= (s\circ q)\circ M &\\ (Ass) & s\circ q\circ r= (s\circ q)\circ r &\\ (IdR) & s\circ id= s &\\ (IdShift) & id\circ \mathcal{W}=\mathcal{W} &\\ (ConsShift) & \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}= s &\\ (Map) & s\circ \langle q\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle=\langle s\circ q \,,\, s\circ N\diagdown x\rangle &\\ (\alpha) & \lambda x.M=\lambda y.\langle\mathcal{W}\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ M & (x,y \text{ are arbitrary})\\ [5pt] \end{array}$
nodes.statement_short: Draft equational theory (Beta, Abs, App, ConsVar, New, IdVar, Clos, Ass, IdR, IdShift, ConsShift, Map, $\alpha$) for named explicit substitutions.
nodes.label: rav

nodes.name: Derived equation $(\mathcal{W})$
nodes.statement: The following special case of $(\alpha)$ is important $$ \begin{array}{ll} \lambda x.y=\lambda x.\langle\mathcal{W}\,,\, x\diagdown x\rangle\circ y & \quad(x\not\equiv y)\\ [5pt] \end{array}$$ Applying $New$ to the right part, we obtain\\ $ \begin{array}{lccc} \quad(\mathcal{W})& \qquad & \lambda x.y=\lambda x.\mathcal{W}\circ y & \quad(x\not\equiv y)\\ [5pt] \end{array}$
nodes.statement_short: Specializing $(\alpha)$ to a variable $y\neq x$ and applying New gives $\lambda x.y=\lambda x.\mathcal{W}\circ y$.

nodes.name: Example 1.10 (computing $(\lambda xy.x)y$ in the calculus of equations)
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} (\lambda x y.x)\,y & \\ = \langle id\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ \lambda y.x & Beta\\ =\lambda y.\langle\mathcal{W}\circ \langle id\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, y\diagdown y\rangle\circ x & Abs\\ =\lambda y.(\mathcal{W}\circ \langle id\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle)\circ x & New\\ =\lambda y.\langle\mathcal{W}\circ id\,,\, \mathcal{W}\circ y\diagdown x\rangle\circ x & Map\\ = \lambda y.\mathcal{W}\circ y & ConsVar\\ =\lambda z.\langle\mathcal{W}\,,\, z\diagdown y\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}\circ y & \alpha\\ =\lambda z.(\langle\mathcal{W}\,,\, z\diagdown y\rangle\circ \mathcal{W})\circ y & Clos\\ =\lambda z.\mathcal{W}\circ y & ConsShift\\ =\lambda z.y & \mathcal{W} \end{array} $$
nodes.statement_short: Step-by-step equational computation of $(\lambda xy.x)\,y=\lambda z.y$, including a renaming of the bound variable.
nodes.label: primer

nodes.name: Example 1.11 (typing derivation with $\mathcal{W}_x$)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{x:A,x:B\vdash \mathcal{W}_x\triangleright x:A}{x:A\vdash x:A}{x:A,x:B\vdash \mathcal{W}_x\circ x:A} $$

nodes.name: Example 1.12 (typing derivation with $\mathcal{W}_y\circ\mathcal{W}_x$)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{x:A,x:B,y:C\vdash \mathcal{W}_y\triangleright x:A,x:B}{x:A,x:B\vdash \mathcal{W}_x\triangleright x:A}{x:A,x:B,y:C\vdash\mathcal{W}_y\circ\mathcal{W}_x\triangleright x:A}}{x:A\vdash x:A}{x:A,x:B,y:C\vdash (\mathcal{W}_y\circ\mathcal{W}_x)\circ x:A} $$

nodes.statement_short: Rewrite rules of the subscripted-$\mathcal{W}$ calculus, including $\mathcal{W}_1$, $\mathcal{W}_2$ and the renaming rule $\alpha_1$ under a freshness side condition.

nodes.name: Example 1.14 (reducing $(\lambda xy.x)y$ in $\lambda\mathcal{W}$)
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} (\lambda x y.x)\,y & \\ \rightarrow\langle id\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ \lambda y.x & Beta\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ \langle id\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, y\diagdown y\rangle\circ x & Abs\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.(\mathcal{W}_y\circ \langle id\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle)\circ x & New\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ id\,,\, \mathcal{W}_y\circ y\diagdown x\rangle\circ x & Map\\ \rightarrow \lambda y.\mathcal{W}_y\circ y & ConsVar\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\langle\mathcal{W}_z\,,\, z\diagdown y\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_y\circ y & \alpha_1\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.(\langle\mathcal{W}_z\,,\, z\diagdown y\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_y)\circ y & Clos\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\mathcal{W}_z\circ y & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.y & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array} $$
nodes.statement_short: Reduction of $(\lambda xy.x)\,y$ to $\lambda z.y$ using Beta, Abs, New, Map, ConsVar, $\alpha_1$, Clos, ConsShift, $\mathcal{W}_1$.
nodes.label: primer2

nodes.name: Well-formed terms and substitutions (introductory)
nodes.statement: (Well-formed terms and substitutions).\\ $ \begin{array}{lll} (i)& \Gamma,x\vdash x &\\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{\Gamma\vdash x}{\Gamma,y\vdash x} & (x\not\equiv y) \\[15pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash MN} &\\[15pt] (iv)& \ruleone{\Gamma,x\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda x.M} &\\[15pt] (v)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}{\Delta\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash s\circ M} &\\[15pt] (vi)& \Gamma\vdash id\triangleright\Gamma &\\[5pt] (vii)& \Gamma,x\vdash\mathcal{W}_{x} \triangleright\Gamma &\\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\triangleright\Delta ,x} &\\[15pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}{\Delta\vdash q\triangleright\Sigma}{\Gamma\vdash s\circ q\triangleright\Sigma} & \end{array} $

nodes.name: Compatible closure
nodes.statement: (Compatible closure).\\[10pt] $ \begin{array}{ccc} & \ruleone{ M_1\rightarrow M_2}{ \lambda x.M_1\rightarrow\lambda x.M_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ M_1\rightarrow M_2}{ M_1N\rightarrow M_2N} & \ruleone{ N_1\rightarrow N_2}{ MN_1\rightarrow MN_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ s_1\rightarrow s_2}{s_1\circ M\rightarrow s_2\circ M} & \ruleone{ M_1\rightarrow M_2}{s\circ M_1\rightarrow s\circ M_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ s_1\rightarrow s_2}{ \langle s_1\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\rightarrow \langle s_2\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle} & \ruleone{ N_1\rightarrow N_2}{ \langle s\,,\, N_1\diagdown x\rangle\rightarrow \langle s\,,\, N_2\diagdown x\rangle}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ s_1\rightarrow s_2}{ s_1\circ q\rightarrow s_2\circ q} & \ruleone{ q_1\rightarrow q_2}{ s\circ q_1\rightarrow s\circ q_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{M_1\rightarrow M_2}{\Gamma\vdash M_1\rightsquigarrow \Gamma\vdash M_2}\\[20pt] \end{array} $

nodes.name: Terms and substitutions (metavariables)
nodes.statement: The symbols $x,y,z,\ldots$ are \emph{variables}. The symbols $M,N,L$ range over \emph{terms}, $s,q,r$ range over \emph{substitutions}, and $a,b,c$ range over variables (they are \emph{metavariables}). The sets of terms and substitutions are defined inductively as follows: \begin{align*} M,N::&= a \mid MN \mid \lambda a. M \mid s\circ M\\ s,q::&= id \mid \mathcal{W}_{a} \mid \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a \rangle \mid s\circ q \end{align*} Note that\\[5pt] $\begin{array}{llll} s\circ M & \text{corresponds to} & M[s] &\text{ from ~\cite{Abadi}};\\ s\circ q & \text{corresponds to} & q\circ s &\text{ from ~\cite{Abadi}};\\ \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle & \text{corresponds to} & N\cdot s &\text{ from ~\cite{Abadi}};\\ \mathcal{W}_{a} & \text{corresponds to} & \uparrow &\text{ from ~\cite{Abadi}}. \end{array}$\\
nodes.statement_short: Grammar of terms ($a$, $MN$, $\lambda a.M$, $s\circ M$) and substitutions ($id$, $\mathcal{W}_a$, $\langle s, N\diagdown a\rangle$, $s\circ q$), with correspondence to $\lambda\sigma$ notation.
nodes.label: pervoe

nodes.name: Parenthesis conventions
nodes.statement: Outermost parentheses are not written.\\ Outermost parentheses around $s$ in $\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle$ are not written.\\ Outermost parentheses around $N$ in $\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle$ are not written.
nodes.label: notation2

nodes.name: Shorthand conventions for terms and substitutions
nodes.statement: $ $\\[3pt] $\begin{array}{lll} MN_1\ldots N_k & \text{is shorthand for} & ((MN_1)\ldots)N_k\\ \lambda a_1\ldots a_k.M & \text{is shorthand for} & \lambda a_1.(\ldots(\lambda a_k.M))\\ \lambda a.MN_1\ldots N_k & \text{is shorthand for} & \lambda a.(MN_1\ldots N_k)\\ s\circ MN_1\ldots N_k & \text{is shorthand for} & s\circ(MN_1\ldots N_k)\\ \lambda a.s\circ M & \text{is shorthand for} & \lambda a.(s\circ M)\\ s\circ \lambda a.M & \text{is shorthand for} & s\circ(\lambda a.M)\\ s_1\circ\ldots\circ s_k\circ s_{k+1} & \text{is shorthand for} & s_1\circ(\ldots\circ(s_k\circ s_{k+1}))\\ s_1\circ \ldots\circ s_k\circ M & \text{is shorthand for} & s_1\circ(\ldots\circ(s_k\circ M))\\ \langle s\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\, \ldots\,,\, N_n\diagdown b_n \rangle & \text{is shorthand for} & \langle\langle\ldots\langle\langle s\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\rangle\,,\, N_2\diagdown b_2\rangle\,,\,\ldots\rangle\,,\, N_n\diagdown b_n\rangle \end{array}$
nodes.statement_short: Association conventions: application to the left, abstraction and closure to the right, nested conses flattened.
nodes.label: notation1

nodes.name: Context
nodes.statement: A \emph{context} is a possibly empty, finite list of variables with multiplicity (i.e., repetitions are permitted). The symbols $\Gamma,\Delta,\Sigma,\Psi$ range over contexts.
nodes.genus: a possibly empty, finite list of variables

nodes.name: Example 2.11 (context $x,x,y$)
nodes.statement: The list $x,x,y$ is a context.

nodes.name: Judgement
nodes.statement: A \emph{judgement} is an expression of the form $\Gamma\vdash M$ or of the form $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$.

nodes.name: Inference rules for judgements
nodes.statement: (The inference rules for judgements).\\ $ \begin{array}{lll} (i)& \Gamma,a\vdash a &\\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{\Gamma\vdash a}{\Gamma,b\vdash a} & (a\neq b) \\[15pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash MN} &\\[15pt] (iv)& \ruleone{\Gamma,a\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.M} &\\[15pt] (v)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}{\Delta\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash s\circ M} &\\[15pt] (vi)& \Gamma\vdash id\triangleright\Gamma &\\[5pt] (vii)& \Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a} \triangleright\Gamma &\\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Delta ,a} &\\[15pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}{\Delta\vdash q\triangleright\Sigma}{\Gamma\vdash s\circ q\triangleright\Sigma} & \end{array} $\\
nodes.statement_short: Nine inference rules deriving well-formed terms $\Gamma\vdash M$ and substitutions $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$.
nodes.label: defsequentsder

nodes.name: Example 2.14 (derivation)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{x,x,y\vdash \mathcal{W}_y\triangleright x,x}{\ruletwo{x,x\vdash \mathcal{W}_x\triangleright x}{x\vdash x}{x,x\vdash \mathcal{W}_x\circ x}}{x,x,y\vdash \mathcal{W}_y\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x} $$

nodes.name: Example 2.15 (derivation)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma,x\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda x.M}}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash (\lambda x.M)N} $$

nodes.name: Example 2.16 (derivation)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash id\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash\langle id\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\triangleright\Gamma,x}}{\ruledot{\Gamma,x\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\langle id\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\circ M} $$

nodes.name: Generation lemma
nodes.statement: $ $\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma,a\vdash a$ is an application of the rule~(i).\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma,b\vdash a$ $($where $a\neq b)$ is an application of the rule~(ii) to some derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash a$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash MN$ is an application of the rule~(iii) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash M$ and $\,\Gamma\vdash N$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash \lambda a.M$ is an application of the rule~(iv) to some derivation of $\,\Gamma,a\vdash M$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\circ M$ is an application of the rule~(v) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ and $\,\Delta\vdash M$ for some $\Delta$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash id\triangleright\Delta$ is an application of the rule~(vi), where $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Delta\vdash \mathcal{W}_{a}\triangleright\Gamma$ is an application of the rule~(vii), where $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma,a$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Sigma$ is an application of the rule~(viii) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ and $\,\Gamma\vdash N$ for some $\Delta$, where $\Sigma$ coincides with $\Delta,a$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\circ q\triangleright\Sigma$ is an application of the rule~(ix) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ and $\,\Delta\vdash q\triangleright\Sigma$ for some $\Delta$.
conclusions: Each derivation of $\,\Gamma,a\vdash a$ is an application of the rule~(i)
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma,b\vdash a$ $($where $a\neq b)$ is an application of the rule~(ii) to some derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash a$
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash MN$ is an application of the rule~(iii) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash M$ and $\,\Gamma\vdash N$
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash \lambda a.M$ is an application of the rule~(iv) to some derivation of $\,\Gamma,a\vdash M$
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\circ M$ is an application of the rule~(v) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ and $\,\Delta\vdash M$ for some $\Delta$
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash id\triangleright\Delta$ is an application of the rule~(vi), where $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma$
Each derivation of $\,\Delta\vdash \mathcal{W}_{a}\triangleright\Gamma$ is an application of the rule~(vii), where $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma,a$

Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Sigma$ is an application of the rule~(viii) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ and $\,\Gamma\vdash N$ for some $\Delta$, where $\Sigma$ coincides with $\Delta,a$

Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\circ q\triangleright\Sigma$ is an application of the rule~(ix) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ and $\,\Delta\vdash q\triangleright\Sigma$ for some $\Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Every derivation of a judgement ends with the unique inference rule matching the judgement's outermost form.

nodes.name: Proof of the Generation lemma
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward.
nodes.statement_short: Straightforward inspection of the inference rules.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.18 (target context of a substitution is unique)
nodes.statement: If a judgement of the form $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ is derivable, then $\Delta$ is uniquely defined for given $\Gamma$ and $s$.
assumptions: a judgement of the form $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ is derivable
conclusions: $\Delta$ is uniquely defined for given $\Gamma$ and $s$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.18
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the structure of $s$ (see Definition~\ref{pervoe}).\\ Case 1: $s$ is $id$. This implies that $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma$.\\ Case 2: $s$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{a}$ for some $a$. This implies that $\Gamma$ coincides with $\Delta,a$.\\ Case 3: $s$ has the form $\langle q\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle$ for some $q,N,a$. By Generation lemma, we can derive $\Gamma\vdash q\triangleright\Sigma$ for some $\Sigma$. By the induction hypothesis, $\Sigma$ is uniquely defined for $\Gamma$ and $q$. Then $\Delta$ coincides with $\Sigma,a$.\\ Case 4: $s$ has the form $q\circ r$ for some $q,r$. By Generation lemma, we can derive $\Gamma\vdash q\triangleright\Sigma$ for some $\Sigma$. By the induction hypothesis, $\Sigma$ is uniquely defined for $\Gamma$ and $q$. By Generation lemma, we can derive $\Sigma\vdash r\triangleright\Delta$, where $\Delta$ is uniquely defined for $\Sigma$ and $r$.
nodes.statement_short: Structural induction on $s$ with four cases, using the Generation lemma.

nodes.name: Induction on $s$
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the structure of $s$ (see Definition~\ref{pervoe}).\\
nodes.statement_short: Set up structural induction on $s$.

nodes.name: Case $s=id$
nodes.statement: Case 1: $s$ is $id$. This implies that $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma$.\\
nodes.statement_short: If $s$ is $id$, $\Delta$ is $\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Case $s=\mathcal{W}_a$
nodes.statement: Case 2: $s$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{a}$ for some $a$. This implies that $\Gamma$ coincides with $\Delta,a$.\\
nodes.statement_short: If $s$ is $\mathcal{W}_a$, $\Gamma$ is $\Delta,a$.

nodes.name: Case cons
nodes.statement: Case 3: $s$ has the form $\langle q\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle$ for some $q,N,a$. By Generation lemma, we can derive $\Gamma\vdash q\triangleright\Sigma$ for some $\Sigma$. By the induction hypothesis, $\Sigma$ is uniquely defined for $\Gamma$ and $q$. Then $\Delta$ coincides with $\Sigma,a$.\\
nodes.statement_short: Cons case via the Generation lemma and the induction hypothesis.

nodes.name: Case composition
nodes.statement: Case 4: $s$ has the form $q\circ r$ for some $q,r$. By Generation lemma, we can derive $\Gamma\vdash q\triangleright\Sigma$ for some $\Sigma$. By the induction hypothesis, $\Sigma$ is uniquely defined for $\Gamma$ and $q$. By Generation lemma, we can derive $\Sigma\vdash r\triangleright\Delta$, where $\Delta$ is uniquely defined for $\Sigma$ and $r$.
nodes.statement_short: Composition case via the Generation lemma applied twice.

nodes.name: Unique derivation lemma
nodes.statement: For any derivable judgement, there is a unique derivation.

nodes.name: Decidability of derivability
nodes.statement: The problem of derivability for judgements is decidable.
conclusions: The problem of derivability for judgements is decidable

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.20
nodes.statement: We try to construct a derivation from the bottom up.
nodes.statement_short: Bottom-up construction of a derivation.

nodes.statement: Not each term is well-formed in any context. A term of the form $\lambda a.\mathcal{W}_{b}\circ M $ is not well-formed in any context if $a\neq b$. $$ \ruleone{\ruletwo{\Gamma,y\vdash \mathcal{W}_y\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash M}}{\Gamma,x\vdash \mathcal{W}_y\circ M \using(?)}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda x.\mathcal{W}_y\circ M} $$

nodes.name: Example 2.22 (not well-formed)
nodes.statement: A term of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ M)(\mathcal{W}_{b}\circ N)$ is not well-formed in any context if $a\neq b$. $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma,x\vdash\mathcal{W}_x\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash M}}{\Gamma,x\vdash\mathcal{W}_x\circ M}} {\ruletwo{\Gamma,y\vdash\mathcal{W}_y\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma,y\vdash\mathcal{W}_y\circ N}} {?\vdash(\mathcal{W}_x\circ M)(\mathcal{W}_y\circ N)} $$

nodes.statement: A substitution of the form $\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{b}$ is not well-formed in any contexts if $a\neq b$. $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\triangleright\Delta,x}}{\Delta,y\vdash\mathcal{W}_y\triangleright\Delta\using(?)}{\Gamma\vdash\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_y\triangleright\Delta} $$
nodes.label: bedsubst

nodes.name: Level of a free occurrence
nodes.statement: Consider some term $M$ and some variable $a$. To each free occurrence of $a$ in $M$ assign its \emph{level}, which is a natural number $\geqslant 1$.

nodes.name: Sequences of sets and their union
nodes.statement: The symbols $\mathcal{A,B}$ range over infinite sequences of sets $$\langle \mathcal{A}_1,\mathcal{A}_2,\mathcal{A}_3,\ldots\rangle\in Sets^\omega$$ $$\langle \mathcal{B}_1,\mathcal{B}_2,\mathcal{B}_3,\ldots\rangle\in Sets^\omega$$ By $\mathcal{A}\cup\mathcal{B}$ denote $$\langle\mathcal{A}_1\cup\mathcal{B}_1,\mathcal{A}_2\cup\mathcal{B}_2,\mathcal{A}_3\cup\mathcal{B}_3,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: Free-variable sequence $FV(L)$
nodes.statement: To each term $L$ we assign an infinite sequence of sets $$FV(L)\equiv\langle FV_1(L),FV_2(L),FV_3(L),\ldots\rangle\in Sets^\omega$$ The variables from the set $FV_i(L)$ have free occurrences of level $i$ in $L$.

nodes.name: Set of free variables
nodes.statement: The set of free variables of $L$ is $\bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(L)$.

nodes.name: Free variables of terms
nodes.statement: (Free variables of terms). By definition, put\\ $ \begin{array}{ll} (i) & FV(a)=\langle \{a\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle\\ (ii) & FV(MN)=FV(M)\cup FV(N)\\ (iii) & FV(\lambda a.M)=O_{\lambda a}(FV(M))\\ (iv) & FV(s\circ M)=O_s(FV(M)), \end{array} $\\[5pt] where\\[5pt] $ \begin{array}{ll} (v) & O_{\lambda a}(\mathcal{A})= \langle(\mathcal{A}_1\setminus\{a\})\cup\mathcal{A}_2\,,\mathcal{A}_3,\mathcal{A}_4,\ldots\rangle\\ (vi) & O_{id}(\mathcal{A})=\mathcal{A}\\ (vii) & O_{\mathcal{W}_{a}}(\mathcal{A})=\langle\emptyset,\mathcal{A}_1,\mathcal{A}_2,\ldots\rangle\\ (viii) & O_{s\circ q}(\mathcal{A})=O_s(O_{q}(\mathcal{A}))\\ (ix) & O_{\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle}(\mathcal{A})=O_s(O_{\lambda a}(\mathcal{A}))\cup FV(N) \end{array}$
nodes.statement_short: Defines $FV(M)$ level-wise via operators $O_{\lambda a}$, $O_{id}$, $O_{\mathcal{W}_a}$ (shift up a level), $O_{s\circ q}$ and $O_{\langle s,N\diagdown a\rangle}$.
nodes.label: FV

nodes.name: Corollary 3.3 (free-variable equations)
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $ \begin{array}{l} FV_1(\lambda a.M)=(FV_1(M)\setminus\{a\})\cup FV_2(M)\\ FV_{n+1}(\lambda a.M)=FV_{n+2}(M)\quad (n\geqslant 1)\\ FV(id\circ M)= FV(M)\\ FV_1(\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ M)=\emptyset \\ FV_{n+1}(\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ M)= FV_{n}(M)\quad (n\geqslant 1)\\ FV(\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ M)= O_s(O_{\lambda a}(FV(M)))\cup FV(N) \end{array} $
conclusions: $ \begin{array}{l} FV_1(\lambda a.M)=(FV_1(M)\setminus\{a\})\cup FV_2(M)\\ FV_{n+1}(\lambda a.M)=FV_{n+2}(M)\quad (n\geqslant 1)\\ FV(id\circ M)= FV(M)\\ FV_1(\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ M)=\emptyset \\ FV_{n+1}(\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ M)= FV_{n}(M)\quad (n\geqslant 1)\\ FV(\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ M)= O_s(O_{\lambda a}(FV(M)))\cup FV(N) \end{array} $
nodes.statement_short: Explicit level-wise formulas for $FV$ of abstractions, $id\circ M$, $\mathcal{W}_a\circ M$ and $\langle s,N\diagdown a\rangle\circ M$.

nodes.name: Abstraction over a context $\lambda\Gamma.M$
nodes.statement: We define $\lambda\Gamma.M$ as follows: \\ $ \begin{array}{ll} & \lambda\,nil.M \equiv M\\ & \lambda\Sigma,a.M \equiv\lambda\Sigma.(\lambda a.M), \end{array} $\\[5pt] where $nil$ is the empty context. For example, $$\lambda x,y,z.M\equiv\lambda xyz.M$$

nodes.name: Free variables of judgements
nodes.statement: (Free variables of judgements). By definition, put\\ $ \begin{array}{ll} & FV(\Gamma\vdash M)=FV(\lambda\Gamma.M)\\ \end{array} $

nodes.name: Lifting $\Uparrow_{\Delta}(s)$
nodes.statement: We define $\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(s)$ as follows: \\ $ \begin{array}{ll} & \Uparrow_{nil}(s) \equiv s\\ & \Uparrow_{\Sigma,a}(s) \equiv\langle\mathcal{W}_{a}\,\circ\Uparrow_{\Sigma}\!(s)\,,\, a\diagdown a\rangle, \end{array} $\\[5pt] where $nil$ is the empty context. For example, $$\Uparrow_{x,y,z}\!(s)\equiv\langle\mathcal{W}_{z}\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_{y}\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_{x}\circ s\,,\, x\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, y\diagdown y\rangle\,,\, z\diagdown z\rangle$$
nodes.statement_short: Recursive lifting of a substitution under a context: $\Uparrow_{\Sigma,a}(s)=\langle\mathcal{W}_a\circ\Uparrow_\Sigma(s), a\diagdown a\rangle$.
nodes.label: uparrow

nodes.name: Lifting decomposes
nodes.statement: Note that $\Uparrow_{\Sigma,a}\!(s)\equiv\,\Uparrow_{a}\!\!(\Uparrow_{\Sigma}\!(s))$.

nodes.name: Convention for $\Uparrow_{\Delta}$ of a cons
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $ \begin{array}{lll} \Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle & \text{is shorthand for} & \Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle) \end{array} $

nodes.name: Reflexive transitive closures
nodes.statement: By $\rightarrow\rightarrow$ denote the reflexive transitive closure of $\rightarrow$.\\ By $\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow$ denote the reflexive transitive closure of $\rightsquigarrow$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.5 (lookup through a cons list)

nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle id\,,\, N\diagdown x\,,\, L\diagdown x\rangle\circ x & \\ \rightarrow L & ConsVar \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Example 4.10
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle id\,,\, N\diagdown x\,,\, L\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \\ \rightarrow(\langle id\,,\, N\diagdown x\,,\, L\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_x)\circ x & Clos\\ \rightarrow \langle id\,,\, N\diagdown x\rangle\circ x & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow N & ConsVar \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Example 4.11
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle \mathcal{W}_x\,,\, N\diagdown y\,,\, L\diagdown y\rangle\circ z & \\ \rightarrow\langle \mathcal{W}_x\,,\, N\diagdown y\rangle\circ z & New\\ \rightarrow\mathcal{W}_x\circ z & New\\ \rightarrow z & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Example 4.12 ($\mathcal{W}_x\circ x$ is a normal form)
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle\mathcal{W}_x\,,\, N\diagdown y\,,\, L\diagdown y\rangle\circ x & \\ \rightarrow\langle\mathcal{W}_x\,,\, N\diagdown y\rangle\circ x & New\\ \rightarrow\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & New \end{array}$$ where $\mathcal{W}_x\circ x$ is a normal form.

nodes.name: Example 4.14 ($\alpha_1$-renaming of $\lambda x.\mathcal{W}_x\circ x$)
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \lambda x.\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \alpha_1\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.(\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_x)\circ x & Clos\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\mathcal{W}_y\circ x & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.x & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Example 4.16 (alternative reduction of $(\lambda xy.x)y$)
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} (\lambda x y.x)\,y & \\ \rightarrow \langle id\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ\lambda y.x & Beta\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ\langle id\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, y\diagdown y\rangle\circ x & Abs\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ id\,,\, \mathcal{W}_y\circ y\diagdown x\,,\, y\diagdown y\rangle\circ x & Map\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ id\,,\, \mathcal{W}_y\circ y\diagdown x\rangle\circ x & New\\ \rightarrow \lambda y.\mathcal{W}_y\circ y & ConsVar\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\langle\mathcal{W}_z\,,\, z\diagdown y\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_y\circ y & \alpha_1\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.(\langle\mathcal{W}_z\,,\, z\diagdown y\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_y)\circ y & Clos\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\mathcal{W}_z\circ y & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.y & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Example 4.17
nodes.statement: $FV(x\vdash\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)=FV(\lambda x.\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)=\langle\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$

nodes.name: Example 4.18 ($\alpha_2$ on a judgement)
nodes.statement: $$ x,x\vdash \mathcal{W}_x\circ x \rightsquigarrow_{\alpha_2} x,y\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_x\circ x$$ Further, $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle \mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \\ \rightarrow (\langle \mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_x)\circ x & Clos\\ \rightarrow \mathcal{W}_y\circ x & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow x & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array}$$ We see that $$\begin{array}{ll} x,x\vdash \mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \\ \rightsquigarrow x,y\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \alpha_2\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y\vdash (\langle \mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}_x)\circ x & Clos\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y\vdash \mathcal{W}_y\circ x & ConsShift\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y\vdash x & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Example 4.19
nodes.statement: $FV(\lambda x z.\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)=\langle\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$

nodes.name: Example 4.20 ($\alpha_1$ followed by Abs with lifting)
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \lambda x x z.\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \\ \rightarrow \lambda x y.\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ\lambda z.\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \alpha_1\\ \rightarrow \lambda x y z.\Uparrow_z\!\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & Abs\\ \equiv\lambda x y z.\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, z\diagdown z\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \rightarrow \lambda x y z.(\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, z\diagdown z\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_z)\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & Clos\\ \rightarrow \lambda x y z.(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle)\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow \lambda x y z.\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\,,\,\mathcal{W}_z\circ y\diagdown x\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & Map\\ \rightarrow \lambda x y z.(\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\,,\,\mathcal{W}_z\circ y\diagdown x\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_x)\circ x & Clos\\ \rightarrow \lambda x y z.(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y)\circ x & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow \lambda x y z.\mathcal{W}_z\circ x & \mathcal{W}_2\\ \rightarrow \lambda x y z. x & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: Reduction of $\lambda xxz.\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x$ to $\lambda xyz.x$ via $\alpha_1$, Abs and the lifting $\Uparrow_z$.

nodes.name: Example 4.21
nodes.statement: $FV(x,z\vdash\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)=FV(\lambda x z.\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)=\langle\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$

nodes.name: Example 4.22 ($\alpha_2$ with lifting)
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} x,x,z\vdash\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \\ \rightsquigarrow x,y,z\vdash\,\Uparrow_z\!\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & \alpha_2\\ \equiv x,y,z\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, z\diagdown z\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y,z\vdash(\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, z\diagdown z\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_z)\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & Clos\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y,z\vdash(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_y\,,\, y\diagdown x\rangle)\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & ConsShift\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y,z\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\,,\,\mathcal{W}_z\circ y\diagdown x\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x & Map\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y,z\vdash(\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\,,\,\mathcal{W}_z\circ y\diagdown x\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_x)\circ x & Clos\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y,z\vdash(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y)\circ x & ConsShift\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y,z\vdash\mathcal{W}_z\circ x & \mathcal{W}_2\\ \rightsquigarrow x,y,z\vdash x & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: The judgement $x,x,z\vdash\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_x\circ x$ reduces to $x,y,z\vdash x$ via $\alpha_2$ and $\sigma$-style rules.

nodes.name: Example 4.23 (reducing $SK$-style term $(\lambda xyz.xz(yz))(\lambda xy.x)$)
nodes.statement: (Some redexes are underlined).\\ $$\begin{array}{ll} (\lambda x y z.xz(yz))(\lambda x y.x) & \\ \rightarrow \langle id\,,\, \lambda x y.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ\lambda y z.xz(yz) & Beta\\ \rightarrow \lambda y.\Uparrow_{y}\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda x y.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ\lambda z. xz(yz) & Abs\\ \rightarrow \lambda y z.\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda x y.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ xz(yz) & Abs\\ \rightarrow \lambda y z.(\underline{\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda x y.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ xz})\,(\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda x y.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ yz) & App\\ \rightarrow\rightarrow \lambda y z.(\lambda x y.x)\,z\,(\underline{\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda x y.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ yz}) & App, Example~\ref{4.25},Example~\ref{4.26}\\ \rightarrow\rightarrow \lambda y z.(\lambda x y.x)\,z\,(yz) & App,Example~\ref{4.27},Example~\ref{4.26}\\ \rightarrow \lambda y z.(\langle id\,,\, z\diagdown x\rangle\circ\lambda y.x)(yz) & Beta\\ \rightarrow \lambda y z.(\lambda y.\underline{\Uparrow_y\!\langle id\,,\, z\diagdown x\rangle\circ x})(yz) & Abs\\ \rightarrow\rightarrow \lambda y z.(\lambda y. z)(yz) & Example~\ref{4.28}\\ \rightarrow \lambda y z.\langle id\,,\, yz\diagdown y\rangle\circ z & Beta\\ \rightarrow \lambda y z.id\circ z & New\\ \rightarrow \lambda y z.z & IdVar \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: Reduction of $(\lambda xyz.xz(yz))(\lambda xy.x)$ to $\lambda yz.z$, delegating sub-reductions to Examples 4.24-4.27.

nodes.name: Example 4.24
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \Uparrow_{y,z}\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ x & \\ \equiv\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\Uparrow_y\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, y\diagdown y\rangle\circ x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \rightarrow(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\Uparrow_y\! \langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle)\circ x & New\\ \equiv(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ \langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, y\diagdown y\rangle)\circ x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \rightarrow\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\circ\langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, \mathcal{W}_z\circ y\diagdown y\rangle\circ x & Map\\ \rightarrow(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\circ\langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle)\circ x & New\\ \rightarrow(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ id\,,\, \mathcal{W}_y\circ\lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle)\circ x & Map\\ \rightarrow\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\circ id\,,\,\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\circ\lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ x & Map\\ \rightarrow\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\circ\lambda xy.x & ConsVar\\ \rightarrow\rightarrow \lambda x y.x & because\,\, \lambda xy.x\,\, is\,\, closed \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Example 4.25
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \Uparrow_{y,z}\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ z & \\ \equiv\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ \Uparrow_y\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, z\diagdown z\rangle\circ z & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \rightarrow z & ConsVar \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Example 4.26
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \Uparrow_{y,z}\!\langle id\,,\,\lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\circ y & \\ \equiv\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\Uparrow_y\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, z\diagdown z\rangle\circ y & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \rightarrow(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\Uparrow_y\!\langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle)\circ y & New\\ \equiv(\mathcal{W}_z\circ\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ\langle id\,,\,\lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, y\diagdown y\rangle)\circ y & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \rightarrow\langle\mathcal{W}_z\circ\mathcal{W}_y\circ\langle id\,,\, \lambda xy.x\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, \mathcal{W}_z\circ y\diagdown y\rangle\circ y & Map\\ \rightarrow \mathcal{W}_z\circ y & ConsVar\\ \rightarrow y & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Example 4.27
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \Uparrow_y\!\langle id\,,\, z\diagdown x\rangle\circ x & \\ \equiv\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ\langle id\,,\, z\diagdown x\rangle\,,\, y\diagdown y\rangle\circ x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \rightarrow(\mathcal{W}_y\circ\langle id\,,\, z\diagdown x\rangle)\circ x & New\\ \rightarrow\langle\mathcal{W}_y\circ id\,,\,\mathcal{W}_y\circ z\diagdown x\rangle\circ x & Map\\ \rightarrow\mathcal{W}_y\circ z & ConsVar\\ \rightarrow z & \mathcal{W}_1 \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Subject reduction, part one
nodes.statement: $ $\\ If $\Gamma\vdash M_1$ is derivable and $M_1\rightarrow M_2$, then $\Gamma\vdash M_2$ is derivable.\\ If $\Gamma\vdash s_1\triangleright\Delta$ is derivable and $s_1\rightarrow s_2$, then $\Gamma\vdash s_2\triangleright\Delta$ is derivable.
nodes.label: SubRed1

nodes.name: Proof of Subject reduction, part one
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward, but tedious.\\[5pt] Case $Beta. \quad (\lambda a.M)N\rightarrow \langle id\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ M $\\[5pt] $$\ruletwo{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.M}}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash (\lambda a.M)N}$$\\[5pt] $$\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash id\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash\langle id\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Gamma,a}}{\ruledot{\Gamma,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\langle id\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}$$\\[5pt] Case $Abs. \quad s\circ \lambda a.M\rightarrow\lambda a.\langle \mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\,,\, a\diagdown a\rangle\circ M $\\[5pt] $$\ruletwo{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}}{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Delta,a\vdash M}}{\Delta\vdash\lambda a.M}}{\Gamma\vdash s\circ\lambda a.M}$$\\[5pt] $$\ruleone{\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a}\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}}{\Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\triangleright\Delta}}{\Gamma,a\vdash a}{\Gamma,a\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\,,\, a\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Delta,a}}{\ruledot{\Delta,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma,a\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\,,\, a\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.\langle\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\,,\, a\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}$$\\[5pt] Case $\alpha_1$. $ \lambda a.M\rightarrow\lambda b.\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M $ $\quad (*)$ \\[5pt] $$\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.M}$$\\[5pt] $$\ruleone{\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma,b\vdash\mathcal{W}_{b}\triangleright\Gamma}{\Gamma,b\vdash b}{\Gamma,b\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Gamma,a}}{\ruledot{\Gamma,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma,b\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda b.\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}$$\\[5pt] And so on. Note that we do not use $(*)$ in the proof of the case $\alpha_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on the reduction rule, exhibiting a derivation of the reduct (cases Beta, Abs, $\alpha_1$ shown).

nodes.name: Case Beta
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward, but tedious.\\[5pt] Case $Beta. \quad (\lambda a.M)N\rightarrow \langle id\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ M $\\[5pt] $$\ruletwo{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.M}}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash (\lambda a.M)N}$$\\[5pt] $$\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash id\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash\langle id\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Gamma,a}}{\ruledot{\Gamma,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\langle id\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}$$\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Exhibit derivations of the Beta-redex and its reduct.

nodes.name: Case Abs
nodes.statement: Case $Abs. \quad s\circ \lambda a.M\rightarrow\lambda a.\langle \mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\,,\, a\diagdown a\rangle\circ M $\\[5pt] $$\ruletwo{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}}{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Delta,a\vdash M}}{\Delta\vdash\lambda a.M}}{\Gamma\vdash s\circ\lambda a.M}$$\\[5pt] $$\ruleone{\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a}\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta}}{\Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\triangleright\Delta}}{\Gamma,a\vdash a}{\Gamma,a\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\,,\, a\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Delta,a}}{\ruledot{\Delta,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma,a\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\,,\, a\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.\langle\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ s\,,\, a\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}$$\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Exhibit derivations of the Abs-redex and its reduct.

nodes.name: Case $\alpha_1$
nodes.statement: Case $\alpha_1$. $ \lambda a.M\rightarrow\lambda b.\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M $ $\quad (*)$ \\[5pt] $$\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.M}$$\\[5pt] $$\ruleone{\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma,b\vdash\mathcal{W}_{b}\triangleright\Gamma}{\Gamma,b\vdash b}{\Gamma,b\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Gamma,a}}{\ruledot{\Gamma,a\vdash M}}{\Gamma,b\vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda b.\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M}$$\\[5pt] And so on. Note that we do not use $(*)$ in the proof of the case $\alpha_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Exhibit derivations for $\alpha_1$; remaining cases are similar and $(*)$ is not needed.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2 (Abs preserves derivability)
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash s\circ\lambda a.M$ is derivable, then $\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.\!\Uparrow_{a}\!(s) \circ M$ is derivable.
nodes.label: lemma1.2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{SubRed1}, the case $Abs$.
nodes.statement_short: The Abs case of Subject reduction, part one.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.3 (iterated Abs preserves derivability)
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash s\circ\lambda\Delta.M$ is derivable, then $\Gamma\vdash\lambda \Delta.\!\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(s)\circ M$ is derivable.
nodes.label: lemma31

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3
nodes.statement: Recall that $\Uparrow_{\Sigma,a}\!(s)\equiv\,\Uparrow_{a}\!\!(\Uparrow_{\Sigma}\!(s))$. Now we can use Lemma~\ref{lemma1.2} repeatedly.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 5.2 repeatedly, using $\Uparrow_{\Sigma,a}=\Uparrow_a\circ\Uparrow_\Sigma$.

nodes.name: Subject reduction, part two
nodes.statement: $ $\\ Suppose\\ $\Gamma,a,\Delta\vdash M$ is derivable and\\ $\Gamma,a,\Delta\vdash M\rightsquigarrow_{\alpha_2} \Gamma,b,\Delta\vdash\, \Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M$;\\ then\\ $\Gamma,b,\Delta\vdash\, \Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M$ is derivable.
nodes.statement_short: An $\alpha_2$-step (renaming a context variable) preserves derivability.

nodes.name: Proof of Subject reduction, part two
nodes.statement: By Generation lemma $\Gamma,a,\Delta\vdash M$ is derivable iff $\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.\lambda\Delta.M$ is derivable. To conclude the proof, it is sufficient to prove the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce via the Generation lemma to derivability of $\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.\lambda\Delta.M$, then apply Lemma 5.5.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.5 (renaming under abstraction preserves derivability)
nodes.statement: Suppose\\ $\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.\lambda\Delta.M$ is derivable; then\\ $\Gamma\vdash\lambda b.\lambda\Delta.\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M$ is derivable.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.5
nodes.statement: We use Theorem~\ref{SubRed1} (the case $\alpha_1$) and Lemma~\ref{lemma31}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the $\alpha_1$ case of Subject reduction with Lemma 5.3.

nodes.name: The calculus $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$
nodes.statement: By $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$ denote $\lambda\mathcal{W}$ without $Beta$.

nodes.name: Composite weakening $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$
nodes.statement: By $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$ denote $(\ldots((\mathcal{W}_{a_1}\circ\mathcal{W}_{a_2})\circ\ldots)\circ\mathcal{W}_{a_n}$

nodes.name: Normal forms of substitutions
nodes.statement: Suppose $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ is derivable and $s$ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form (with respect to $\rightarrow$); then $s$ has one of the following forms:\\ $ \begin{array}{lll} (i) & id &\\ (ii) & \mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n} & (n\geqslant 1)\\ (iii) & \langle id\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle & (k\geqslant 1)\\ (iv) & \langle\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle & (n\geqslant 1, k\geqslant 1) \end{array} $\\
conclusions: $s$ has one of the following forms
nodes.statement_short: A derivable $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal substitution is $id$, a composite weakening, or a cons list over one of these.
nodes.label: Subnf

nodes.name: Components of normal substitutions are normal
nodes.statement: Of course, the terms $N_1,\ldots,N_k$ are not arbitrary, they are $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal forms (with respect to $\rightarrow$).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.3
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the structure of $s$ (see Definition~\ref{pervoe}). The set of substitutions of the forms $(i)-(iv)$ contains $id$ and $\mathcal{W}_{a}$ for any $a$. This set is also closed under $\langle - \,,\, N\diagdown b\rangle$ for any $N,b$. To conclude the proof, it is sufficient to prove the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the structure of $s$; the forms (i)-(iv) are closed under cons, and composition is handled by Lemma 6.4.

nodes.name: Induction on $s$
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the structure of $s$ (see Definition~\ref{pervoe}).
nodes.statement_short: Set up structural induction on $s$.

nodes.name: Base and cons cases
nodes.statement: The set of substitutions of the forms $(i)-(iv)$ contains $id$ and $\mathcal{W}_{a}$ for any $a$. This set is also closed under $\langle - \,,\, N\diagdown b\rangle$ for any $N,b$.
nodes.statement_short: The forms (i)-(iv) contain $id$ and $\mathcal{W}_a$ and are closed under cons.

nodes.name: Reduce to Lemma 6.4
nodes.statement: To conclude the proof, it is sufficient to prove the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: The composition case reduces to the following lemma.

nodes.name: Lemma 6.4 (composition of normal substitutions)
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash s\circ q\triangleright\Delta$ is derivable and both $s,q$ belong to $(i),(ii),(iii),(iv)$, then $s\circ q\,$ $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-reduces to one of the forms $(i),(ii),(iii),(iv)$.
conclusions: $s\circ q\,$ $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-reduces to one of the forms $(i),(ii),(iii),(iv)$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.4
nodes.statement: Let us considered five cases. \\[5pt] Case 1: $q$ is $id$.\\ $s\circ id\rightarrow s$\\[5pt] Case 2: $s$ is $id$ and $q$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$.\\ $id\circ \mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}\rightarrow\rightarrow \mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\\[5pt] Case 3: $s$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$ and $q$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$.\\ $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n})\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}\rightarrow\rightarrow \mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_nc_1\ldots c_m}$\\[5pt] Case 4: $s$ has the form $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle$ and $q$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$, where $r$ is $id$ or $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$. Hence, $s\circ q$ has the form\\ $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$. By Generation lemma, $b_k= c_1$,\\ $b_{k-1}= c_2$, and so on (see Example~\ref{bedsubst}). \\[5pt] If $k=m$,\,then\\[5pt] $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\quad is the same as\\ $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{b_k\ldots b_1}\rightarrow\rightarrow r$\\[5pt] If $k>m$,\,then \\[5pt] $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\quad is the same as\\ $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{b_k\ldots b_{k-m+1}}\rightarrow\rightarrow \langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_{k-m}\diagdown b_{k-m}\rangle $\\[5pt] If $k<m$,\,then\\[5pt] $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\quad is the same as\\ $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown c_k\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown c_1\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\\ If $r$ is $id$, this term reduces to $\mathcal{W}_{c_{k+1}\ldots c_m}$. If $r$ is $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$, this term reduces to $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_nc_{k+1}\ldots c_m}$.\\[5pt] Case 5: $q$ has the form $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle$, where $r$ is $id$ or $\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$.\\ $s\circ\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\rightarrow\rightarrow\langle s\circ r\,,\, s\circ N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, s\circ N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle$\\ Then we use the previous cases to reduce $s\circ r$.
nodes.statement_short: Five-way case analysis on the shapes of $s$ and $q$; the cons-versus-weakening case uses the Generation lemma to match variables and compares $k$ with $m$.

nodes.name: Five cases
nodes.statement: Let us considered five cases. \\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Announce a five-way case analysis.

nodes.name: Case $q=id$
nodes.statement: Case 1: $q$ is $id$.\\ $s\circ id\rightarrow s$\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: IdR.

nodes.name: Case $id\circ\mathcal{W}$
nodes.statement: Case 2: $s$ is $id$ and $q$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$.\\ $id\circ \mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}\rightarrow\rightarrow \mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: IdShift-type reduction.

nodes.name: Case weakening composed with weakening
nodes.statement: Case 3: $s$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$ and $q$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$.\\ $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n})\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}\rightarrow\rightarrow \mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_nc_1\ldots c_m}$\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Composite weakenings concatenate.

nodes.name: Case cons composed with weakening
nodes.statement: Case 4: $s$ has the form $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle$ and $q$ has the form $\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$, where $r$ is $id$ or $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$. Hence, $s\circ q$ has the form\\ $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$. By Generation lemma, $b_k= c_1$,\\ $b_{k-1}= c_2$, and so on (see Example~\ref{bedsubst}). \\[5pt] If $k=m$,\,then\\[5pt] $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\quad is the same as\\ $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{b_k\ldots b_1}\rightarrow\rightarrow r$\\[5pt] If $k>m$,\,then \\[5pt] $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\quad is the same as\\ $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{b_k\ldots b_{k-m+1}}\rightarrow\rightarrow \langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_{k-m}\diagdown b_{k-m}\rangle $\\[5pt] If $k<m$,\,then\\[5pt] $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\quad is the same as\\ $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown c_k\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown c_1\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$\\ If $r$ is $id$, this term reduces to $\mathcal{W}_{c_{k+1}\ldots c_m}$. If $r$ is $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$, this term reduces to $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_nc_{k+1}\ldots c_m}$.\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Generation lemma matches variables; compare $k$ and $m$ and cancel by ConsShift.

nodes.name: Case composition with a cons
nodes.statement: Case 5: $q$ has the form $\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle$, where $r$ is $id$ or $\mathcal{W}_{c_1\ldots c_m}$.\\ $s\circ\langle r\,,\, N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle\rightarrow\rightarrow\langle s\circ r\,,\, s\circ N_1\diagdown b_1\,,\,\ldots\,,\, s\circ N_k\diagdown b_k\rangle$\\ Then we use the previous cases to reduce $s\circ r$.
nodes.statement_short: Map, then reduce $s\circ r$ by previous cases.

nodes.name: Lemma 6.4 does not use $\mathcal{W}_1,\mathcal{W}_2,\alpha_1,\alpha_2$
nodes.statement: Note that we do not use $\mathcal{W}_1,\mathcal{W}_2,\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ in this proof.

nodes.name: Pure term
nodes.statement: A term $M$ is called \emph{pure} iff it does not contain sub-terms of the shape $s\circ N$.
differentia: it does not contain sub-terms of the shape $s\circ N$

nodes.name: Normal forms are pure
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable and $\Gamma\vdash M$ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form (with respect to $\rightsquigarrow$), then $M$ is pure.
assumptions: $\Gamma\vdash M$ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form (with respect to $\rightsquigarrow$)
nodes.label: pure

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.6
nodes.statement: Suppose $M$ contain a sub-term of the shape $s\circ N$; then $N$ must be a variable (we denote it by $b$), else we can apply $Abs, App$ or $Clos$. The substitution $s$ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form and must have the form $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$ (see theorem~\ref{Subnf}), else we can apply $IdVar, ConsVar$ or $New$. Further, $a_n$ in $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n})\circ b$ must coincide with $b$, else we can apply $\mathcal{W}_1$ or $\mathcal{W}_2$. We see that $M$ must be constructed from variables and blocks of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b\quad (m\geqslant 0)$ by using application and abstraction. To conclude the proof, it is sufficient to prove the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Any closure in a normal form must be a block $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$ by Theorem 6.3; Lemma 6.7 shows such blocks admit $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$.

nodes.name: Closure must act on a variable
nodes.statement: Suppose $M$ contain a sub-term of the shape $s\circ N$; then $N$ must be a variable (we denote it by $b$), else we can apply $Abs, App$ or $Clos$.
nodes.statement_short: Any closure $s\circ N$ in a normal form has $N$ a variable, else Abs, App or Clos applies.

nodes.name: Substitution is a composite weakening
nodes.statement: The substitution $s$ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form and must have the form $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$ (see theorem~\ref{Subnf}), else we can apply $IdVar, ConsVar$ or $New$.
nodes.statement_short: By Theorem 6.3, $s$ must be $\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n}$.

nodes.name: Last subscript matches
nodes.statement: Further, $a_n$ in $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_n})\circ b$ must coincide with $b$, else we can apply $\mathcal{W}_1$ or $\mathcal{W}_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise $\mathcal{W}_1$ or $\mathcal{W}_2$ applies.

nodes.name: Shape of $M$
nodes.statement: We see that $M$ must be constructed from variables and blocks of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b\quad (m\geqslant 0)$ by using application and abstraction.
nodes.statement_short: So $M$ is built from variables and blocks by application and abstraction.

nodes.name: Reduce to Lemma 6.7
nodes.statement: To conclude the proof, it is sufficient to prove the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to prove the following lemma.

nodes.name: Lemma 6.7 (blocks can be renamed away)
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable and $M$ is constructed from variables and blocks of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b\quad(m\geqslant 0)$ by using application and abstraction, then $M$ is pure (this means that $M$ does not contain blocks) or we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash M$.
assumptions: $M$ is constructed from variables and blocks of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b\quad(m\geqslant 0)$ by using application and abstraction
conclusions: $M$ is pure (this means that $M$ does not contain blocks) or we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash M$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.7
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the structure of $M$. Let us consider four cases.\\[5pt] Case 1: $M$ is a variable. The proof is trivial.\\[5pt] Case 2: $ M$ has the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma\vdash M$ has the form\\ $\Delta\,,\,b\,,\,a_m\,,\,\ldots\,,\, a_1\vdash (\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$ \\ and we can apply $\alpha_2$ , because\\ $FV(b\,,\,a_m\,,\,\ldots\,,\, a_1\vdash (\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b)=\langle\{b\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$\\[10pt] Case 3: $M$ has the form $\lambda a.N$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma,a\vdash N$ is derivable. Suppose $N$ contains a block of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$. By induction hypothesis, we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma,a\vdash N$. But any application of $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma,a\vdash N$ corresponds to some application of $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ (and, in some cases, $Abs$) to $\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.N$. For example,\\ $\Gamma,a\vdash N\rightsquigarrow_{\alpha_2}\Gamma,b \vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ N$\\ corresponds to\\ $\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.N\rightsquigarrow_{\alpha_1}\Gamma\vdash\lambda b.\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ N$\\[10pt] Case 4: $M$ has the form $NL$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma\vdash N$ and $\Gamma\vdash L$ are derivable. Suppose one of these terms contains a block of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$. For clarity, let it be $N$. By induction hypothesis, we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash N$. I claim that we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash NL$. For the case $\alpha_1$ is nothing to prove, because any $\alpha_1$-redex in $N$ occurs in $NL$ too. For the case $\alpha_2$, suppose that $\Gamma\vdash NL$ has the form $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash NL$. Recall that $FV(NL)=FV(N)\cup FV(L)$, hence $FV(N)\subseteq FV(NL)$. By Lemma~\ref{monotone},\\ $FV(a,\Delta\vdash N))\subseteq FV(a,\Delta\vdash NL)$.\\ Hence if $a\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(a,\Delta\vdash N)$, then $a\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(a,\Delta\vdash NL)$. If we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash N$, then we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash NL$.
nodes.statement_short: Structural induction on $M$ with four cases. The application case uses monotonicity of $FV$ to lift an $\alpha_2$-redex from $N$ to $NL$.

nodes.name: Induction on $M$
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the structure of $M$. Let us consider four cases.\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Structural induction on $M$, four cases.

nodes.name: Case variable
nodes.statement: Case 1: $M$ is a variable. The proof is trivial.\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Trivial.

nodes.name: Case block
nodes.statement: Case 2: $ M$ has the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma\vdash M$ has the form\\ $\Delta\,,\,b\,,\,a_m\,,\,\ldots\,,\, a_1\vdash (\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$ \\ and we can apply $\alpha_2$ , because\\ $FV(b\,,\,a_m\,,\,\ldots\,,\, a_1\vdash (\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b)=\langle\{b\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$\\[10pt]
nodes.statement_short: A block admits $\alpha_2$ since its variable is free at level 1.

nodes.name: Case abstraction
nodes.statement: Case 3: $M$ has the form $\lambda a.N$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma,a\vdash N$ is derivable. Suppose $N$ contains a block of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$. By induction hypothesis, we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma,a\vdash N$. But any application of $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma,a\vdash N$ corresponds to some application of $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ (and, in some cases, $Abs$) to $\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.N$. For example,\\ $\Gamma,a\vdash N\rightsquigarrow_{\alpha_2}\Gamma,b \vdash\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ N$\\ corresponds to\\ $\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.N\rightsquigarrow_{\alpha_1}\Gamma\vdash\lambda b.\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ N$\\[10pt]
nodes.statement_short: Redexes in the body lift to $\alpha_1$/$\alpha_2$ (and Abs) on $\lambda a.N$.

nodes.name: Case application
nodes.statement: Case 4: $M$ has the form $NL$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma\vdash N$ and $\Gamma\vdash L$ are derivable. Suppose one of these terms contains a block of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$. For clarity, let it be $N$. By induction hypothesis, we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash N$. I claim that we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash NL$. For the case $\alpha_1$ is nothing to prove, because any $\alpha_1$-redex in $N$ occurs in $NL$ too. For the case $\alpha_2$, suppose that $\Gamma\vdash NL$ has the form $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash NL$. Recall that $FV(NL)=FV(N)\cup FV(L)$, hence $FV(N)\subseteq FV(NL)$. By Lemma~\ref{monotone},\\ $FV(a,\Delta\vdash N))\subseteq FV(a,\Delta\vdash NL)$.\\ Hence if $a\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(a,\Delta\vdash N)$, then $a\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(a,\Delta\vdash NL)$. If we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash N$, then we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash NL$.
nodes.statement_short: Lift a renaming redex from $N$ to $NL$.

nodes.name: Apply induction hypothesis to $N$
nodes.statement: Case 4: $M$ has the form $NL$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma\vdash N$ and $\Gamma\vdash L$ are derivable. Suppose one of these terms contains a block of the form $(\mathcal{W}_{a_1\ldots a_mb})\circ b$. For clarity, let it be $N$. By induction hypothesis, we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash N$.
nodes.statement_short: By the Generation lemma and induction hypothesis, $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ applies to $\Gamma\vdash N$.

nodes.name: Claim: renaming applies to $NL$
nodes.statement: I claim that we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash NL$. For the case $\alpha_1$ is nothing to prove, because any $\alpha_1$-redex in $N$ occurs in $NL$ too. For the case $\alpha_2$, suppose that $\Gamma\vdash NL$ has the form $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash NL$. Recall that $FV(NL)=FV(N)\cup FV(L)$, hence $FV(N)\subseteq FV(NL)$. By Lemma~\ref{monotone},\\ $FV(a,\Delta\vdash N))\subseteq FV(a,\Delta\vdash NL)$.\\ Hence if $a\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(a,\Delta\vdash N)$, then $a\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(a,\Delta\vdash NL)$. If we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash N$, then we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash NL$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim that $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ applies to $\Gamma\vdash NL$.

nodes.name: Subcase $\alpha_1$
nodes.statement: For the case $\alpha_1$ is nothing to prove, because any $\alpha_1$-redex in $N$ occurs in $NL$ too.
nodes.statement_short: An $\alpha_1$-redex in $N$ occurs in $NL$.

nodes.name: Subcase $\alpha_2$
nodes.statement: For the case $\alpha_2$, suppose that $\Gamma\vdash NL$ has the form $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash NL$. Recall that $FV(NL)=FV(N)\cup FV(L)$, hence $FV(N)\subseteq FV(NL)$. By Lemma~\ref{monotone},\\ $FV(a,\Delta\vdash N))\subseteq FV(a,\Delta\vdash NL)$.\\
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 3.20, $FV$ of the judgement with $N$ is included in that with $NL$.

nodes.name: Side condition transfers
nodes.statement: Hence if $a\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(a,\Delta\vdash N)$, then $a\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(a,\Delta\vdash NL)$. If we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash N$, then we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,a,\Delta\vdash NL$.
nodes.statement_short: So the $\alpha_2$ side condition holds for $NL$.

nodes.name: Normal substitutions may contain impure terms
nodes.statement: Warning! In general, the terms $N_1,\ldots,N_k$ in the statement of Theorem~\ref{Subnf} are not pure. For example, the judgement\\ $x,x\vdash\langle id\,,\,\mathcal{W}_x\circ x\diagdown y\rangle\triangleright x,x,y$\\ is derivable and the substitution\\ $\langle id\,,\,\mathcal{W}_x\circ x\diagdown y\rangle$\\ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form.

nodes.name: Name-free terms and substitutions
nodes.statement: The symbols $U,V,W$ range over \emph{name-free terms} and the symbols $u,v,w$ range over \emph{name-free substitutions}. The sets of name-free terms and name-free substitutions are defined inductively as follows: \begin{align*} U,V::&= 1 \mid UV \mid \lambda U \mid u\circ U \\ u,v::&= id \mid \mathcal{W} \mid \langle u\,,\, V \rangle \mid u\circ v \end{align*}

nodes.name: The calculus $\lambda\sigma$ (in the new notation)
nodes.statement: (The calculus $\lambda\sigma$ in the new notation).\\[10pt] $ \begin{array}{ccc} & \ruleone{ U_1\rightarrow U_2}{ \lambda U_1\rightarrow\lambda U_2} &\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ U_1\rightarrow U_2}{ U_1V\rightarrow U_2V} & \ruleone{ V_1\rightarrow V_2}{ UV_1\rightarrow UV_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ u_1\rightarrow u_2}{u_1\circ U\rightarrow u_2\circ U} & \ruleone{ U_1\rightarrow U_2}{u\circ U_1\rightarrow u\circ U_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ u_1\rightarrow u_2}{ \langle u_1\,,\, V \rangle\rightarrow \langle u_2\,,\, V\rangle} & \ruleone{ V_1\rightarrow V_2}{ \langle u\,,\, V_1 \rangle\rightarrow \langle u\,,\, V_2\rangle}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ u_1\rightarrow u_2}{ u_1\circ v\rightarrow u_2\circ v} & \ruleone{ v_1\rightarrow v_2}{ u\circ v_1\rightarrow u\circ v_2}\\[20pt] \end{array} $ $ \begin{array}{lll} (Beta) & (\lambda U)V\rightarrow \langle id\,,\, V\rangle\circ U &\\ (Abs) & u\circ \lambda U\rightarrow\lambda \langle \mathcal{W}\circ u\,,\, 1\rangle\circ U &\\ (App) & u\circ UV\rightarrow(u\circ U)(u\circ V) &\\ (ConsVar) & \langle u\,,\, V\rangle\circ 1\rightarrow V &\\ (IdVar) & id\circ 1\rightarrow 1 &\\ (Clos) & u\circ v\circ V\rightarrow (u\circ v)\circ V &\\ (Ass) & u\circ v\circ w\rightarrow (u\circ v)\circ w &\\ (IdR) & u\circ id\rightarrow u &\\ (IdShift) & id\circ \mathcal{W}\rightarrow\mathcal{W} &\\ (ConsShift) & \langle u\,,\, V\rangle\circ \mathcal{W}\rightarrow u &\\ (Map) & u\circ \langle v\,,\, V\rangle\rightarrow\langle u\circ v \,,\, u\circ V\rangle & \end{array} $\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: The de Bruijn explicit-substitution calculus $\lambda\sigma$ of Abadi et al., rewritten with reversed composition.

nodes.name: The calculus $\sigma$ and $\sigma$-normal form $\sigma(U)$
nodes.statement: By $\sigma$ denote $\lambda\sigma$ without $Beta$.\\ By $\sigma(U)$ denote the $\sigma$-normal form of $U$ (this normal form exists and is uniquely defined because $\sigma$ is strongly normalizing and confluent).

nodes.name: De Bruijn numerals $\underline{n}$
nodes.statement: By definition, put\\ $\underline{n}\equiv\underbrace{((\ldots(\mathcal{W}\circ\mathcal{W})\circ\ldots)\circ\mathcal{W})}_{\mbox{\scriptsize $n-1$ times}}\circ 1 \qquad(n\geqslant 1)$

nodes.name: Numeral identities
nodes.statement: We see that $\underline{1}\equiv 1$, $\underline{2}\equiv\mathcal{W}\circ 1$, and $\underline{n+1}\equiv\sigma(\mathcal{W}\circ\underline{n})$.

nodes.name: Name-free term corresponding to a judgement (notation)
nodes.statement: $(\Gamma\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U$ is shorthand for ``the name-free term $U$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash M$."\\ $(\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u$ is shorthand for ``the name-free substitution $u$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$."

nodes.name: Rules of correspondence between judgements and name-free terms
nodes.statement: (The rules of correspondence between judgements and name-free terms/substitutions).\\[5pt] $ \begin{array}{ll} (i)& (\Gamma,a\vdash a)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} 1 \\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{(\Gamma\vdash a)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \underline{n}}{(\Gamma,b\vdash a)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \underline{n+1}\using {\quad(a\neq b)}}\\[20pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U}{(\Gamma\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } V}{(\Gamma\vdash MN)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} UV}\\[15pt] (iv)& \ruleone{(\Gamma,a\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } U}{(\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \lambda U}\\[15pt] (v)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \triangleright\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u }{(\Delta\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } U}{(\Gamma\vdash s \circ M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } u \circ U}\\[15pt] (vi)& (\Gamma\vdash id \triangleright\Gamma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} id \\[5pt] (vii)& (\Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a} \triangleright\Gamma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \mathcal{W} \\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \triangleright\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u }{(\Gamma\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} V}{(\Gamma\vdash \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle \triangleright\Delta ,a)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \langle u\,,\, V\rangle }\\[15pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \triangleright\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u }{(\Delta\vdash q \triangleright\Sigma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} v }{(\Gamma \vdash s \circ q \triangleright\Sigma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u \circ v }\\[20pt] \end{array} $
nodes.statement_short: Translation of derivable judgements into name-free ($\lambda\sigma$) terms and substitutions, by induction on derivations.
nodes.label: transfer

nodes.name: Example 7.7 (translation to name-free)
nodes.statement: $$ (x\vdash x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} 1 $$

nodes.name: Example 7.8 (translation to name-free)

nodes.statement: $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable by Lemma~\ref{poleznaya}. $\Sigma\vdash L$ is derivable by Subject reduction. Therefore $L$ is pure and $V$ is a $\sigma$-normal form (Theorem~\ref{pure}, Lemma~\ref{purelemma}).

nodes.statement: Why $U\overset{\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}V$? It is sufficient to prove that $\sigma(U)\equiv\sigma(V)$ ($U$ reduces to its $\sigma$-normal form because $\sigma$ is strongly normalizing and confluent).

nodes.name: Induction on length
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the length of the reduction sequence $ \Gamma\vdash M\overset{\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma\vdash L$. If this length is equal to $0$, there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, suppose this sequence has the form \\ $\Gamma\vdash M\rightsquigarrow\ldots\rightsquigarrow\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow\Sigma\vdash L$,\\ where $(\Delta\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}W$ and $\sigma(U)\equiv\sigma(W)$.\\
