nodes.name: Rules shared with $\sigma$ and renaming rules
nodes.statement: Any possible $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-reduction step $\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow\Sigma\vdash L$, except $New,\mathcal{W}_1,\mathcal{W}_2,\alpha_1$, and $\alpha_2$ corresponds to the same name $\sigma$-reduction step of the nameless terms $W\rightarrow V$, hence $\sigma(W)\equiv\sigma(V)$ in these cases. For $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ use Lemma~\ref{lemmauparrow}.\\
nodes.statement_short: Shared rules correspond to $\sigma$-steps; $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ handled by Lemma 7.17.

nodes.name: Case $\mathcal{W}_1$
nodes.statement: (\textbf{Case} $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{W}_1}.) \quad \mathcal{W}_{a}\circ b\rightarrow b \qquad(a\neq b)$ $$\ruletwo{\Gamma,a\vdash \mathcal{W}_{a}\triangleright\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash b}}{\Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ b}\qquad \ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash b}}{\Gamma,a\vdash b}$$ Suppose \\ $(\Gamma\vdash b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\underline{n}$;\\ then\\ $(\Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a}\circ b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\mathcal{W}\circ\underline{n}$ and\\ $(\Gamma,a\vdash b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\underline{n+1}$.\\ We see that $\sigma(\mathcal{W}\circ\underline{n})\equiv\sigma(\underline{n+1})$. \\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Translations agree up to $\sigma$.

nodes.name: Case $\mathcal{W}_2$
nodes.statement: (\textbf{Case} $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{W}_2}.) \quad (s\circ\mathcal{W}_{a})\circ b\rightarrow s\circ b \qquad(a\neq b)$ $$\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\ruledot{\Delta\vdash s\triangleright\Gamma,a}}{\Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a}\triangleright\Gamma}{\Delta\vdash s\circ\mathcal{W}_{a}\triangleright\Gamma}}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash b}}{\Delta\vdash (s\circ\mathcal{W}_{a})\circ b}\qquad \ruletwo{\ruledot{\Delta\vdash s\triangleright\Gamma,a}}{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash b}}{\Gamma,a\vdash b}}{\Delta\vdash s\circ b}$$ Suppose \\ $(\Delta\vdash s\triangleright\Gamma,a)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u$;\\ $(\Gamma\vdash b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\underline{n}$;\\ then\\ $(\Delta\vdash (s\circ\mathcal{W}_{a})\circ b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} (u\circ\mathcal{W})\circ\underline{n}$;\\ $(\Gamma,a\vdash b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \underline{n+1}$;\\ $(\Delta\vdash s\circ b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u\circ\underline{n+1}$.\\ We see that\\ $\sigma((u\circ\mathcal{W})\circ\underline{n})\equiv\sigma(u\circ\underline{n+1})$\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Translations agree up to $\sigma$.

nodes.name: Case New
nodes.statement: (\textbf{Case} ${\mathbf{New}}.) \quad \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ b\rightarrow s\circ b \qquad(a\neq b)$ $$\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\ruledot{\Delta\vdash s\triangleright\Gamma}}{\ruledot{\Delta\vdash N}}{\Delta\vdash\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\triangleright\Gamma,a}}{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash b}}{\Gamma,a\vdash b}}{\Delta\vdash\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ b}\qquad \ruletwo{\ruledot{\Delta\vdash s\triangleright\Gamma}}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash b}}{\Delta\vdash s\circ b}$$ Suppose \\ $(\Delta\vdash s\triangleright\Gamma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u$;\\ $(\Delta\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} V$;\\ $(\Gamma\vdash b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\underline{n}$;\\ then\\ $(\Gamma,a\vdash b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\underline{n+1}$;\\ $(\Delta\vdash\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle\circ b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\langle u\,,\, V\rangle\circ\underline{n+1}$;\\ $(\Delta\vdash s\circ b)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u\circ\underline{n}$.\\ We see that\\ $\sigma(\langle u\,,\, V\rangle\circ\underline{n+1})\equiv\sigma(\langle u\,,\, V\rangle\circ\mathcal{W}\circ\underline{n})\equiv\sigma(u\circ\underline{n})$.
nodes.statement_short: Translations agree up to $\sigma$ via ConsShift.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.22 (Beta projects to $\beta$ on $\sigma$-normal forms)
nodes.statement: If $U\rightarrow_{Beta}V$, then $\sigma(U)\rightarrow^*_{\beta}\sigma(V)$, where $\rightarrow^*_{\beta}$ is the reflexive closure of $\,\rightarrow_{\beta}$.

nodes.statement: See~\cite{Abadi}, Lemma 3.5.

nodes.name: $\lambda\mathcal{W}$-reductions project to $\lambda\sigma$-reductions
nodes.statement: Suppose \\ $\begin{array}{l} \Gamma\vdash M\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma\vdash L;\\ (\Gamma\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U;\\ (\Sigma\vdash L)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} V; \end{array}$\\[5pt] then $\sigma(U)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}\sigma(V)$.
nodes.label: theorem33

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.23
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the length of the reduction sequence $\Gamma\vdash M\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma\vdash L$. If this length is equal to $0$, there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, suppose this sequence has the form \\ $\Gamma\vdash M\rightsquigarrow\ldots\rightsquigarrow\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow\Sigma\vdash L$,\\ where $(\Delta\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} W$ and $\sigma(U)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}\sigma(W)$.\\ If the reduction step $\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow\Sigma\vdash L$ belongs to $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$, everything is all right, because $\sigma(W)\equiv\sigma(V)$ in this case. Indeed, $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable by Lemma~\ref{poleznaya}. $\Delta\vdash N$ and $\Sigma\vdash L$ are derivable by Subject reduction. Take any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Sigma\vdash L$ (this normal form exists by Theorem ~\ref{SN} and are derivable too) and use Theorem~\ref{maintheorem} to get $ W\overset{\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}\sigma(V)$.\\ If $\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow_{Beta}\Sigma\vdash L$, then $W\rightarrow_{Beta}V$, because any $Beta$-redex in $N$ corresponds to some $Beta$-redex in $W$, hence $\sigma(W)\rightarrow^*_{\beta}\sigma(V)$ by Lemma~\ref{lemmapodjom}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the reduction length: $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-steps leave $\sigma(\cdot)$ unchanged (via Theorems 7.19, 7.20), Beta-steps project by Lemma 7.22.

nodes.name: Induction on length
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the length of the reduction sequence $\Gamma\vdash M\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma\vdash L$. If this length is equal to $0$, there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, suppose this sequence has the form \\ $\Gamma\vdash M\rightsquigarrow\ldots\rightsquigarrow\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow\Sigma\vdash L$,\\ where $(\Delta\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} W$ and $\sigma(U)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}\sigma(W)$.\\
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the length of the $\lambda\mathcal{W}$-sequence.

nodes.name: Case $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-step
nodes.statement: If the reduction step $\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow\Sigma\vdash L$ belongs to $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$, everything is all right, because $\sigma(W)\equiv\sigma(V)$ in this case. Indeed, $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable by Lemma~\ref{poleznaya}. $\Delta\vdash N$ and $\Sigma\vdash L$ are derivable by Subject reduction. Take any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Sigma\vdash L$ (this normal form exists by Theorem ~\ref{SN} and are derivable too) and use Theorem~\ref{maintheorem} to get $ W\overset{\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}\sigma(V)$.\\
nodes.statement_short: A $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-step leaves $\sigma(\cdot)$ unchanged, via Theorems 7.20 and 7.19.

nodes.name: Case Beta-step
nodes.statement: If $\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow_{Beta}\Sigma\vdash L$, then $W\rightarrow_{Beta}V$, because any $Beta$-redex in $N$ corresponds to some $Beta$-redex in $W$, hence $\sigma(W)\rightarrow^*_{\beta}\sigma(V)$ by Lemma~\ref{lemmapodjom}.
nodes.statement_short: A Beta-step projects to $\beta$ by Lemma 7.22.

nodes.name: $\lambda\sigma$-reductions lift to $\lambda\mathcal{W}$-reductions
nodes.statement: Suppose \\ $\begin{array}{l} (\Gamma\vdash M) \boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U;\\ U\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}V; \end{array}$\\ then there is $\Sigma\vdash L$ such that\\ $\begin{array}{l} \Gamma\vdash M\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma\vdash L;\\ \Sigma\vdash L \text{ is a } \sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha\text{-normal form (with respect to $\overset{\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}$)};\\ (\Sigma\vdash L)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(V). \end{array}$
nodes.label: theorem44

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.24
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the length of the reduction sequence $U\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}V$. \\[5pt] Case 1: If this length is equal to $0$, take any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Gamma\vdash M$ as $\Sigma\vdash L$ and use Theorem~\ref{maintheorem}. \\[5pt] Case 2: Suppose this sequence has the form $U\rightarrow \ldots\rightarrow W\rightarrow V$ and the sequence $U\rightarrow \ldots\rightarrow W$ satisfies the statement of the theorem, i.e.:\\ $\Gamma\vdash M \overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Delta\vdash N$ for some $\Delta\vdash N$, where $\Delta\vdash N$ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form and $(\Delta\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(W)$.\\[3pt] If the reduction step $W\rightarrow V$ belongs to $\sigma$, everything is all right, because $\sigma(W)\equiv\sigma(V)$ in this case and we can use $\Delta\vdash N$ as $\Sigma\vdash L$. \\[3pt] If $W\rightarrow_{Beta}V$, then $\sigma(W)\rightarrow^*_{\beta}\sigma(V)$ by Lemma~\ref{lemmapodjom}. If $\sigma(W)$ coincides with $\sigma(V)$, everything is all right. Otherwise, suppose $\sigma(W)\rightarrow^*_{\beta}\sigma(V)$ has the form $\sigma(W)\rightarrow_{Beta}W'\overset{\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}\sigma(V)$. Any $Beta$-redex in $\sigma(W)$ corresponds to some $Beta$-redex in $N$. Contracting this redex in $N$, we obtain\\ $\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow_{Beta}\Delta\vdash N'$ and $(\Delta\vdash N')\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}W'$, for some $N'$. Take any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Delta\vdash N'$ as $\Sigma\vdash L$, then use Theorem~\ref{maintheorem} to obtain\\ $(\Sigma\vdash L)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(V)$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the length of the $\lambda\sigma$-sequence; a Beta step on $\sigma(W)$ is mirrored by a Beta step in $N$ followed by $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normalization (Theorem 7.19).

nodes.name: Induction on length
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the length of the reduction sequence $U\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}V$. \\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the length of the $\lambda\sigma$-sequence.

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement: Case 1: If this length is equal to $0$, take any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Gamma\vdash M$ as $\Sigma\vdash L$ and use Theorem~\ref{maintheorem}. \\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Take a normal form and use Theorem 7.19.

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement: Case 2: Suppose this sequence has the form $U\rightarrow \ldots\rightarrow W\rightarrow V$ and the sequence $U\rightarrow \ldots\rightarrow W$ satisfies the statement of the theorem, i.e.:\\ $\Gamma\vdash M \overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Delta\vdash N$ for some $\Delta\vdash N$, where $\Delta\vdash N$ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form and $(\Delta\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(W)$.\\[3pt] If the reduction step $W\rightarrow V$ belongs to $\sigma$, everything is all right, because $\sigma(W)\equiv\sigma(V)$ in this case and we can use $\Delta\vdash N$ as $\Sigma\vdash L$. \\[3pt] If $W\rightarrow_{Beta}V$, then $\sigma(W)\rightarrow^*_{\beta}\sigma(V)$ by Lemma~\ref{lemmapodjom}. If $\sigma(W)$ coincides with $\sigma(V)$, everything is all right. Otherwise, suppose $\sigma(W)\rightarrow^*_{\beta}\sigma(V)$ has the form $\sigma(W)\rightarrow_{Beta}W'\overset{\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}\sigma(V)$. Any $Beta$-redex in $\sigma(W)$ corresponds to some $Beta$-redex in $N$. Contracting this redex in $N$, we obtain\\ $\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow_{Beta}\Delta\vdash N'$ and $(\Delta\vdash N')\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}W'$, for some $N'$. Take any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Delta\vdash N'$ as $\Sigma\vdash L$, then use Theorem~\ref{maintheorem} to obtain\\ $(\Sigma\vdash L)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(V)$.
nodes.statement_short: Extend the lifted sequence by one step.

nodes.name: Induction hypothesis
nodes.statement: Case 2: Suppose this sequence has the form $U\rightarrow \ldots\rightarrow W\rightarrow V$ and the sequence $U\rightarrow \ldots\rightarrow W$ satisfies the statement of the theorem, i.e.:\\ $\Gamma\vdash M \overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Delta\vdash N$ for some $\Delta\vdash N$, where $\Delta\vdash N$ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form and $(\Delta\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(W)$.\\[3pt]
nodes.statement_short: Assume the claim for the prefix ending in $W$.

nodes.name: Case $\sigma$-step
nodes.statement: If the reduction step $W\rightarrow V$ belongs to $\sigma$, everything is all right, because $\sigma(W)\equiv\sigma(V)$ in this case and we can use $\Delta\vdash N$ as $\Sigma\vdash L$. \\[3pt]
nodes.statement_short: Nothing changes.

nodes.name: Case Beta-step
nodes.statement: If $W\rightarrow_{Beta}V$, then $\sigma(W)\rightarrow^*_{\beta}\sigma(V)$ by Lemma~\ref{lemmapodjom}. If $\sigma(W)$ coincides with $\sigma(V)$, everything is all right. Otherwise, suppose $\sigma(W)\rightarrow^*_{\beta}\sigma(V)$ has the form $\sigma(W)\rightarrow_{Beta}W'\overset{\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow}\sigma(V)$. Any $Beta$-redex in $\sigma(W)$ corresponds to some $Beta$-redex in $N$. Contracting this redex in $N$, we obtain\\ $\Delta\vdash N\rightsquigarrow_{Beta}\Delta\vdash N'$ and $(\Delta\vdash N')\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}W'$, for some $N'$. Take any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Delta\vdash N'$ as $\Sigma\vdash L$, then use Theorem~\ref{maintheorem} to obtain\\ $(\Sigma\vdash L)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(V)$.
nodes.statement_short: Mirror the $\beta$-step in $N$ and renormalize, using Lemma 7.22 and Theorem 7.19.

nodes.name: Extended name-free terms and substitutions
nodes.statement: Only in this section, we use the following notation: the symbols $U,V,W$ range over \emph{extended name-free terms} and the symbols $u,v,w$ range over \emph{extended name-free substitutions}. The sets of extended name-free terms and extended name-free substitutions are defined inductively as follows: \begin{align*} U,V::&= \underline{n} \mid UV \mid \lambda U \mid u\circ U \\ u,v::&= id \mid \mathcal{W} \mid \langle u\,,\, V \rangle \mid u\circ v \end{align*} ($n\in N, n\geqslant 1$)

nodes.name: Example 8.2 (extended nameless term)
nodes.statement: $\lambda\lambda\underline{2}(\mathcal{W}\circ\underline{1})$ is an extended nameless term.

nodes.name: Pure extended name-free term
nodes.statement: An extended nameless term $U$ is called \emph{pure} iff it does not contain sub-terms of the form $u\circ U$.

nodes.name: Pure extended terms are built from numerals
nodes.statement: It is clear that any pure term is constructed from the symbols $\underline{n}$ by using application and abstraction.
conclusions: any pure term is constructed from the symbols $\underline{n}$ by using application and abstraction

nodes.name: Name-free judgement
nodes.statement: A \emph{name-free judgement} is an expression of the form $m\vdash U$ or of the form $m\vdash u$, where $m\in N,m\geqslant 0$.

nodes.name: Name-free judgement corresponding to a judgement (notation)
nodes.statement: $(\Gamma\vdash M)\Rightarrow(m\vdash U)$ is shorthand for ``the name-free judgement $m\vdash U$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash M$." \\ $(\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta)\Rightarrow(m\vdash u)$ is shorthand for ``the name-free judgement $m\vdash u$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$."

nodes.name: Length of a context $|\Gamma|$
nodes.statement: By $|\Gamma|$ denote the length of $\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Rules of correspondence between judgements and name-free judgements
nodes.statement: (The rules of correspondence between judgements and name-free judgements).\\ $ \begin{array}{ll} (i)& (\Gamma,a\vdash a)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma,a|\vdash \underline{1}) \\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{(\Gamma\vdash a)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash \underline{n})}{(\Gamma,b\vdash a)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma,b| \vdash \underline{n+1})\using {\quad(a\neq b)}}\\[20pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash M)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash U)}{(\Gamma\vdash N)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash V)}{(\Gamma\vdash MN)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash UV)}\\[15pt] (iv)& \ruleone{(\Gamma,a\vdash M)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma,a| \vdash U)}{(\Gamma\vdash\lambda a.M)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash \lambda U) }\\[15pt] (v)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \triangleright\Delta)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash u) }{(\Delta\vdash M)\Rightarrow (|\Delta| \vdash U)}{(\Gamma\vdash s \circ M)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash u \circ U)}\\[15pt] (vi)& (\Gamma\vdash id \triangleright\Gamma)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash id ) \\[5pt] (vii)& (\Gamma,a\vdash\mathcal{W}_{a} \triangleright\Gamma)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma,a| \vdash \mathcal{W} ) \\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \triangleright\Delta)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash u ) }{(\Gamma\vdash N)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash V)}{(\Gamma\vdash \langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle \triangleright\Delta ,a)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash\langle u\,,\, V\rangle )}\\[15pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \triangleright\Delta)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash u) }{(\Delta\vdash q \triangleright\Sigma)\Rightarrow (|\Delta| \vdash v ) }{(\Gamma \vdash s \circ q \triangleright\Sigma)\Rightarrow (|\Gamma| \vdash u \circ v )}\\ \end{array} $
nodes.statement_short: Translation of judgements into name-free judgements $m\vdash U$ that also record the context length.
nodes.label: deftransfer

nodes.name: Corollary 8.8 (recorded length is the context length)
nodes.statement: If $(\Gamma\vdash M)\Rightarrow(m\vdash U)$, then $m=|\Gamma|$.\\ If $(\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta)\Rightarrow(m\vdash u)$, then $m=|\Gamma|$.

nodes.name: Example 8.9 (translation to name-free judgement)
nodes.statement: $$ (x\vdash x)\Rightarrow (1 \vdash \underline{1}) $$

nodes.name: Example 8.10 (translation to name-free judgement)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruleone{(x\vdash x)\Rightarrow (1 \vdash \underline{1})}{(x,y \vdash x)\Rightarrow (2 \vdash \underline{2})} $$

nodes.name: Example 8.11 (translation to name-free judgement)
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{(x,y \vdash \mathcal{W}_y\triangleright x) \Rightarrow (2 \vdash \mathcal{W})}{(x \vdash x) \Rightarrow (1 \vdash \underline{1})}{(x,y \vdash \mathcal{W}_y\circ x) \Rightarrow (2 \vdash \mathcal{W}\circ \underline{1})} $$

nodes.name: $\alpha$-equivalence
nodes.statement: ($\alpha$-equivalence).\\ We say that $\Gamma\vdash M$ is $\alpha$-\emph{equal} to $\Delta\vdash N$ and write\\ $(\Gamma\vdash M)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Delta\vdash N)$ iff\\ $(\Gamma\vdash M)\Rightarrow (m\vdash U)$ and\\ $(\Delta\vdash N)\Rightarrow (m\vdash U)$, for some $m,U$.
nodes.statement_short: Two judgements are $\alpha$-equal iff they translate to the same name-free judgement $m\vdash U$.

nodes.name: Example 8.13 ($\alpha$-equal judgements)
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $(x,y\vdash\mathcal{W}_y\circ x)\Rightarrow (2\vdash \mathcal{W}\circ \underline{1})$\\ $(x,x\vdash\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)\Rightarrow (2\vdash \mathcal{W}\circ \underline{1})$\\ $(x,y\vdash\mathcal{W}_y\circ x)\equiv_{\alpha} (x,x\vdash\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)$

nodes.name: Example 8.14 ($\alpha$-equal judgements)
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $(x\vdash\lambda y.\mathcal{W}_y\circ x)\Rightarrow (1\vdash \lambda\mathcal{W}\circ \underline{1})$\\ $(x\vdash\lambda x.\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)\Rightarrow (1\vdash \lambda\mathcal{W}\circ \underline{1})$\\ $(x\vdash\lambda y.\mathcal{W}_y\circ x)\equiv_{\alpha} (x\vdash\lambda x.\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)$

nodes.name: Example 8.15 ($\alpha$-equal judgements)
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $(\vdash\lambda x.\lambda y.\mathcal{W}_y\circ x)\Rightarrow (0\vdash \lambda\lambda\mathcal{W}\circ \underline{1})$\\ $(\vdash\lambda x.\lambda x.\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)\Rightarrow (0\vdash \lambda\lambda\mathcal{W}\circ \underline{1})$\\ $(\vdash\lambda x.\lambda y.\mathcal{W}_y\circ x)\equiv_{\alpha} (\vdash\lambda x.\lambda x.\mathcal{W}_x\circ x)$

nodes.name: Alpha-equal terms admit different rules
nodes.statement: Warning! We can apply $\mathcal{W}_1$ to the term $\lambda x.\lambda y.\mathcal{W}_y\circ x$, but not to the term $\lambda x.\lambda x.\mathcal{W}_x\circ x$ (and we can apply $\alpha_1$ to the term $\lambda x.\lambda x.\mathcal{W}_x\circ x$, but not to the term $\lambda x.\lambda y.\mathcal{W}_y\circ x$).

nodes.name: Example 8.16 ($\backsimeq$ does not imply $\equiv_\alpha$)
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $(x,y\vdash x) \backsimeq (x,y\vdash\mathcal{W}_y\circ x)$\\ $(x,y\vdash x)\,{\not\equiv_{\alpha}} (x,y\vdash\mathcal{W}_y\circ x)$
nodes.label: counterexample

nodes.name: Lemma 8.17 (translatable judgements are derivable)
nodes.statement: If $(\Gamma\vdash M)\Rightarrow(m\vdash U)$, then $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.17
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward, see Definition~\ref{defsequentsder} and Definition~\ref{deftransfer}.
nodes.statement_short: Straightforward comparison of the inference and correspondence rules.

nodes.name: Corollary 8.18 ($\alpha$-equal judgements are derivable)
nodes.statement: If $(\Gamma\vdash M)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Delta\vdash N)$, then $\Gamma\vdash M$ and $\Delta\vdash N$ are derivable.

nodes.name: $\alpha$-equivalence versus same name-free translation
nodes.statement: $ $\\ Suppose $(\Gamma\vdash M)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Delta\vdash N)$; then $(\Gamma\vdash M)\backsimeq(\Delta\vdash N)$.\\ Suppose $(\Gamma\vdash M)\backsimeq(\Delta\vdash N)$, where $|\Gamma|=|\Delta|$ and both $M$ and $N$ are pure; then $(\Gamma\vdash M)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Delta\vdash N)$.
assumptions: Suppose $(\Gamma\vdash M)\backsimeq(\Delta\vdash N)$, where $|\Gamma|=|\Delta|$ and both $M$ and $N$ are pure
nodes.label: alpequiv

To prove the second part, recall that each pure term is constructed from variables by using application and abstraction. This prevents such counterexamples as Example~\ref{counterexample}.
nodes.statement_short: First part by comparing the two correspondence definitions; second part because pure terms are built from variables.

nodes.name: First part
nodes.statement: The proof of the first part is straightforward, see Definition~\ref{transfer} and Definition~\ref{deftransfer}.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the two correspondence definitions.

nodes.name: Second part
nodes.statement: To prove the second part, recall that each pure term is constructed from variables by using application and abstraction. This prevents such counterexamples as Example~\ref{counterexample}.
nodes.statement_short: Pure terms are built from variables, ruling out counterexamples.

nodes.name: $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$ is confluent
nodes.statement: Suppose\\ $\begin{array}{l} (\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2);\\ \Gamma_1\vdash M_1\overset{\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Delta_1\vdash N_1;\\ \Gamma_2\vdash M_2\overset{\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Delta_2\vdash N_2; \end{array}$\\ then there are $\Sigma_1\vdash L_1$ and $\Sigma_2\vdash L_2$ such that\\ $\begin{array}{l} \Delta_1\vdash N_1\overset{\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma_1\vdash L_1;\\ \Delta_2\vdash N_2\overset{\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma_2\vdash L_2;\\ (\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2). \end{array}$
nodes.statement_short: Confluence of $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$ up to $\alpha$-equivalence of judgements.
nodes.label: confluence1

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 9.2
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{alpequiv}, we have $(\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\backsimeq(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2)$.\\ Suppose $(\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}U$ and $(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}U$.\\ Let $\Sigma_1\vdash L_1$ be any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Delta_1\vdash N_1$ and let $\Sigma_2\vdash L_2$ be any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Delta_2\vdash N_2$. By Theorem~\ref{maintheorem}, we have\\ $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(U)$ and $(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(U)$, hence\\ $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\backsimeq(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)$. Note that $L_1$ and $L_2$ are pure (Theorem~\ref{pure}). Note that $|\Sigma_1|=|\Sigma_2|=|\Gamma_1|=|\Gamma_2|$ (because all reductions preserve lengths of contexts). By Lemma~\ref{alpequiv}, we have\\ $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Normalize both sides; by Theorem 7.19 both normal forms translate to $\sigma(U)$, are pure, and have equal context lengths, so Lemma 9.1 gives $\alpha$-equality.

nodes.name: Same translation $U$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{alpequiv}, we have $(\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\backsimeq(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2)$.\\ Suppose $(\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}U$ and $(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}U$.\\
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 9.1 both judgements translate to a common $U$.

nodes.name: Normal forms translate to $\sigma(U)$
nodes.statement: Let $\Sigma_1\vdash L_1$ be any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Delta_1\vdash N_1$ and let $\Sigma_2\vdash L_2$ be any $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form of $\Delta_2\vdash N_2$. By Theorem~\ref{maintheorem}, we have\\ $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(U)$ and $(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(U)$, hence\\ $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\backsimeq(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Take normal forms of both reducts; Theorem 7.19 gives both the translation $\sigma(U)$.

nodes.name: Purity and lengths
nodes.statement: Note that $L_1$ and $L_2$ are pure (Theorem~\ref{pure}). Note that $|\Sigma_1|=|\Sigma_2|=|\Gamma_1|=|\Gamma_2|$ (because all reductions preserve lengths of contexts).
nodes.statement_short: Normal forms are pure and contexts have equal length.

nodes.name: Conclude $\alpha$-equality
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{alpequiv}, we have\\ $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9.1 yields $\alpha$-equality.

nodes.name: $\lambda\mathcal{W}$ is confluent
nodes.statement: Suppose\\ $\begin{array}{l} (\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2);\\ \Gamma_1\vdash M_1\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Delta_1\vdash N_1;\\ \Gamma_2\vdash M_2\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Delta_2\vdash N_2; \end{array}$\\ then there are $\Sigma_1\vdash L_1$ and $\Sigma_2\vdash L_2$ such that\\ $\begin{array}{l} \Delta_1\vdash N_1\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma_1\vdash L_1;\\ \Delta_2\vdash N_2\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma_2\vdash L_2;\\ (\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2). \end{array}$
nodes.statement_short: Confluence of $\lambda\mathcal{W}$ up to $\alpha$-equivalence, transferred from the confluence of $\lambda\sigma$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 9.3
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{alpequiv}, we have $(\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\backsimeq(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2)$.\\ Suppose $(\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}U$; $(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}U$;\\ $(\Delta_1\vdash N_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}V_1$; and $(\Delta_2\vdash N_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}V_2$.\\ By Theorem~\ref{theorem33}, we have $\sigma(U)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} \sigma(V_1)$ and $\sigma(U)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} \sigma(V_2)$.\\ We know that $\lambda\sigma$ is confluent, hence $\sigma(V_1)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} V$ and $\sigma(V_2)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} V$ for some $V$. Therefore $V_1\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} V$ and $V_2\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} V$. By Theorem~\ref{theorem44}, we have $\Sigma_1\vdash L_1$ and $\Sigma_2\vdash L_2$ such that\\ $\begin{array}{l} \Delta_1\vdash N_1\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma_1\vdash L_1;\\ \Delta_2\vdash N_2\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma_2\vdash L_2;\\ \Sigma_1\vdash L_1 \text{ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form};\\ \Sigma_2\vdash L_2 \text{ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form};\\ (\Sigma_1\vdash V_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(V);\\ (\Sigma_2\vdash V_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(V). \end{array}$\\[5pt] Hence $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\backsimeq(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)$. Note that $L_1$ and $L_2$ are pure (Theorem~\ref{pure}). Note that $|\Sigma_1|=|\Sigma_2|=|\Gamma_1|=|\Gamma_2|$ (because all reductions preserve lengths of contexts). By Lemma~\ref{alpequiv}, we have\\ $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Project both reductions to $\lambda\sigma$ (Theorem 7.23), join them by confluence of $\lambda\sigma$, lift back (Theorem 7.24), and conclude with Lemma 9.1.

nodes.name: Same translation $U$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{alpequiv}, we have $(\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\backsimeq(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2)$.\\ Suppose $(\Gamma_1\vdash M_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}U$; $(\Gamma_2\vdash M_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}U$;\\ $(\Delta_1\vdash N_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}V_1$; and $(\Delta_2\vdash N_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}V_2$.\\
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 9.1 both judgements translate to a common $U$.

nodes.name: Project reductions
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{theorem33}, we have $\sigma(U)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} \sigma(V_1)$ and $\sigma(U)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} \sigma(V_2)$.\\
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 7.23 projects both reductions to $\lambda\sigma$.

nodes.name: Join in $\lambda\sigma$
nodes.statement: We know that $\lambda\sigma$ is confluent, hence $\sigma(V_1)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} V$ and $\sigma(V_2)\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} V$ for some $V$. Therefore $V_1\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} V$ and $V_2\overset{\lambda\sigma}{\rightarrow\rightarrow} V$.
nodes.statement_short: Confluence of $\lambda\sigma$ gives a common reduct $V$.

nodes.name: Lift back
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{theorem44}, we have $\Sigma_1\vdash L_1$ and $\Sigma_2\vdash L_2$ such that\\ $\begin{array}{l} \Delta_1\vdash N_1\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma_1\vdash L_1;\\ \Delta_2\vdash N_2\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}\Sigma_2\vdash L_2;\\ \Sigma_1\vdash L_1 \text{ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form};\\ \Sigma_2\vdash L_2 \text{ is a $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$-normal form};\\ (\Sigma_1\vdash V_1)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(V);\\ (\Sigma_2\vdash V_2)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\sigma(V). \end{array}$\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 7.24 lifts to $\lambda\mathcal{W}$-reductions to normal forms.

nodes.name: Same translation, pure, equal lengths
nodes.statement: Hence $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\backsimeq(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)$. Note that $L_1$ and $L_2$ are pure (Theorem~\ref{pure}). Note that $|\Sigma_1|=|\Sigma_2|=|\Gamma_1|=|\Gamma_2|$ (because all reductions preserve lengths of contexts).
nodes.statement_short: The normal forms share a translation, are pure, and have equal context lengths.

nodes.name: Conclude $\alpha$-equality
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{alpequiv}, we have\\ $(\Sigma_1\vdash L_1)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Sigma_2\vdash L_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 9.1 yields $\alpha$-equality.

nodes.name: The set $\Lambda\mathcal{W}$
nodes.statement: By $\Lambda\mathcal{W}$ denote the set of derivable judgements of the form $\Gamma\vdash M$.

nodes.name: Confluence on $\Lambda\mathcal{W}$
nodes.statement: We see that $\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}$ and $\overset{\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}$ are confluent (up to $\equiv_{\alpha}$) on the set $\Lambda\mathcal{W}$.
conclusions: $\overset{\lambda\mathcal{W}}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}$ and $\overset{\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha}{\rightsquigarrow\rightsquigarrow}$ are confluent (up to $\equiv_{\alpha}$) on the set $\Lambda\mathcal{W}$

nodes.name: Weak inclusion $\sqsubseteq$ of set sequences
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{A} \sqsubseteq \mathcal{B}$ is shorthand for ``$\mathcal{A}_i\subseteq\bigcup_{j\geqslant i}\mathcal{B}_j$ for all $i\geqslant 1$".

nodes.name: Corollary 10.7 (Abs preserves $FV$)
nodes.statement: $FV(s\circ\lambda a.M)=FV(\lambda a.\!\Uparrow_{a}\!(s) \circ M)$

nodes.statement: $FV(s\circ\lambda \Delta.M)=FV(\lambda \Delta. \!\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(s) \circ M)$

nodes.name: Corollary 10.9 (set of free variables does not grow)
nodes.statement: If $M\rightarrow N$, then $\bigcup_{i\geqslant 1}FV_i(N)\subseteq \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1}FV_i(M)$.

nodes.name: Strong normalization of $R$ implies that of $\sigma\mathcal{W}\alpha$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10.16
nodes.statement:

nodes.name: Size $|M|$, $|s|$
nodes.statement: To each term $M$ and each substitution $s$ we put in correspondence natural numbers $|M|$ and $|s|$ respectively defined as follows:\\ $\begin{array}{l} |\lambda a.M|=|M|+1\\ |\boldsymbol{\lambda} a.M|=|M|+1\\ |s\circ M|=|s|+|M|\\ |s\circ q|=|s|+|q|\\ |MN|=max(|M|,|N|)\\ |\langle s\,,\, N\diagdown a\rangle|=max(|s|,|N|)\\ |id|=0\\ |\mathcal{W}_{a}|=0\\ |a|=0 \end{array}$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10.26
nodes.statement: By choosing the well-founded precedence\\ $ \begin{array}{ll} \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{i+1} a>\circ_i>\boldsymbol{\lambda}_i a & \text{for all } i,a;\\ \circ_i>\lambda a & \text{for all } i,a;\\ \circ_i>\cdot &\text{for all } i;\\ \circ_i>\langle -\,,\, -\diagdown a\rangle & \text{for all } i,a;\\ \circ_i>\mathcal{W}_{a} & \text{for all } i,a;\\ \circ_i> a & \text{for all } i,a;\\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_i a>\lambda b & \text{for all } i,a,b;\\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{i} a>\langle-\,,\, -\diagdown a\rangle & \text{for all } i,a;\\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{i} a>\mathcal{W}_{b} & \text{for all } i,a,b;\\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{i} a> b & \text{for all } i,a,b;\\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_i a>\boldsymbol{\lambda}_j a & \text{for } i>j; \\ \circ_i>\circ_j & \text{for } i>j; \end{array} $\\[5pt] termination is easily proved by the lexicographic path order.
nodes.statement_short: Lexicographic path order with a well-founded precedence on labelled symbols.

nodes.statement: For any infinite $R$-sequence $$M_1\rightarrow M_2\rightarrow M_3\rightarrow\ldots$$ we can get some infinite $Q$-sequence simply by labelling all symbols $\circ$ and $\boldsymbol{\lambda} a$ by theirs own values. nodes.name: Stronger Abs rule
nodes.statement: (1) We can accept $Abs$ in the stronger form\\ $\begin{array}{lll} & s\circ\lambda a.M\rightarrow\lambda b.\langle\mathcal{W}_{b}\circ s\,,\, b\diagdown a\rangle\circ M & (a,b \text{ are arbitrary}) \end{array}$\\[5pt] All results of this article remain true.

nodes.statement: We can also add the following rewrite rules\\ $\begin{array}{ll} & id\circ M\rightarrow M\\ & id\circ s\rightarrow s \end{array}$\\[5pt] All results of this article remain true.

nodes.name: $\alpha$-equivalence for substitutions
nodes.statement: ($\alpha$-equivalence for substitutions).\\ We say that $\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta$ is $\alpha$-\emph{equal} to $\Sigma\vdash q\triangleright\Psi$ and write\\ $(\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta)\equiv_{\alpha}(\Sigma\vdash q\triangleright\Psi)$ iff\\ $(\Gamma\vdash s\triangleright\Delta)\Rightarrow (m\vdash u)$ and\\ $(\Sigma\vdash q\triangleright\Psi)\Rightarrow (m\vdash u)$, for some $m,u$.
